analysis.name: Allison Lamanna
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You are graded on 3 exams so don't skip extra credit if you do not have a background in college biology and chemistry. Covers surface level information, but the amount of topics you learn is a lot so the class is mostly memorization. Lamanna mostly reads off slides, and sometimes incorporates fun activities during lecture to understand concepts.

I really enjoyed Allison's lectures, more than Stuckey's for sure. She did an excellent job at breaking down concepts and reinforced what we needed to know for the tests. For any students about to take this class--DO THE EXTRA CREDIT, it will save your grade. Also the practice tests are very similar to the actual exams and help you succeed.

Attendance was not mandatory, lectures were recorded and posted. Grade is only based on 3 exam scores, so do the extra credit! Lecture slides were very clear with everything you need to know. As long as you know know everything on her practice test and problem sets, you will do good on the exams.

grade is based on three exams, do the extra credit, lamanna is a very confusing lecturer and it was hard to understand what she was talking about and what you need to know for the exams, prior knowledge in chemistry is extremely important to do well on the exams

Somewhat similar to the other professor, but I thought her slides were easier to follow and had everything written out. Sometimes we wouldn't finish in time, so we had to watch recordings, which was pretty annoying. Her practice exams match the actual thing, and as long as you know how to study, this course won't be too bad. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT

analysis.name: Adrian Deva
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Adrian is honestly the best art professor I've ever had. He proves that classes don't need to be stressful and difficult for you to learn a lot. I learned and improved so much in this class mostly because I wasn't stressed out constantly and because Adrian genuinely cares, is super passionate and inspirational, and gives very good advice.

I put lectures cause what he says before you start drawing is really helpful. I feel like my sketching has gotten so much better. This class has been invaluble in my artistic development. Very personable, and says hello outside class. Talks to every single student throughout class. You can make up drawings but its better to draw in class for input.

Probably the best professor I've had so far during my time here. He gives good feedback and plenty of time to do your work. Best part: he doesn't give any homework. Well, except for the final project, but he gives you like a whole month to do that. Highly recommend this professor, very cool and epic

I loved Prof Deva's course. He truly cares about each of his students, and his main priority is always to ensure that you are progressing and developing your skills. Would highly recommend taking a course with him!

Adrian was lovely to have in class! He had so many good insights and I really felt like I learned a lot from him. He was excited to talk about everything he taught and offered us a lot of freedom on the final project.

analysis.name: Aaron Pixton
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 59 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Only a few areas where Pixton could add some clarity to his lectures. However, his method of lecturing worked well for me. Generous with grading; curves of 20-30% to exam scores, waiving quizzes, and incorporating effort into grades. Occasionally appears frustrated when students can't answer his questions in class (maybe somewhat justified lol)

Legend says that he understood the ABC conjecture before anyone else and gave solutions through mystical visions. Some say that he appeared to Shinichi Mochizuki in a dream (he was the one who conceived the entire field of Inter-Universal Teichmuller Theory). Some theorize that he might also be the vision Ramanujan saw before cracking partitions.

When Grass Man Ian attacked the class, Pickstone saved us all. While the sheafs were quasi-coherent, Pickstone was more than coherent. “This is OUR class” he cried, rallying the communist diagrams behind him. Immediately, his magnificent hair rose on its ends and the Grass Man Ian fled in terror. I'm rating him 2 out of 2.
Pickstoneee my loveeee

Pixton is very knowledgeable in math. Sometimes his lectures are just too advanced for undergrads which also is in part the material. He is a generous grader but there lacked some clarity sometimes. Material is hard for the course.

I was trying to draw all the homeomorphically irreducible trees with n = 10 on the board outside class, but I couldn't quite do it.

Pixton was mopping the floors nearby & proceeded to solve it with his mop. I asked him how and he said that my Gordon Wood was good, but I forgot about something called "Vickehs." 

I do like them apples, Aaron!

analysis.name: Hilary Archbold
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor genuinely ignores my emails. I will send questions, and follow ups to those emails because she does not respond. I also am not entirely sure why this lab course is structured in a way that makes it so difficult. This is the first lab class where I need to come to do lab work outside of the 6 HOURS of my week already taken.

Nothing is perfect and even the slightest misunderstanding in either a protocol or an assignment will result in minus points. If you miss a pop quiz then be ready to give up any chance at an A. Additionally, she will make you stay all three hours even if you finish. IN her words "you are mine until the class ends, so you cant go anywhere."

The GSIs were great and labs were interesting, but Dr. Archbold's grading lacked transparency and felt unfair. Her requirements were often very unclear and there were constant point deductions for things never mentioned. She also showed very little understanding or respect for students' personal situations.

I had Dr. Archbold for Genetics over the summer and it was an extremely stressful class. She is never clear when explaining even the most basic of concepts. Exams are extremely difficult and application based. I wouldn't have gotten the grade I did without reading the textbook for a much better explanation. Overall I did not enjoy her.

While she seems kind and I enjoyed the topics, Archbold seemed disorganized at times because she went on too many tangents, leading to her speeding through topics and going over class time. Her handwriting wasn't great either so it was frustrating to follow along in lectures. If you choose to take this class, read the textbook! It made this easier

analysis.name: Michael Andrews
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I went into this class with no experience at all and Michael was able to meet me where I was at and support me along the very steep learning curve. I felt respected, valued and safe in his classes, and he gave me great feedback during our critiques. Michael is a ray of sunshine and I'm so lucky I had the opportunity to meet him!

Nice guy, but emphasizes independent learning to a fault imho. Entire class was structured around one semester-long project, which was not made clear AT ALL in the syllabus btw. Didnt realize what we were in for until it was too late. Class times are used for crits and demos, felt more like formalities. Not what I expected personally, didn't enjoy.

He pushed me to explore a medium I had never tried, that I quite enjoy! I found the structure of the class a little unorganized at first, but overall I thought the class went pretty well. 
It was an 8:30 AM class, and my adhd ass can get loud. There were many times he asked me to quiet down, so if you're loud maybe don't take his classes :,)

I took social spaces and got a 60% participation grade for missing 2 days of class, even though I emailed him every time beforehand. I don't think he allows students to miss a class no matter what. Super unaccommodating with schedule conflict. Uses harsh language during a critique that may be hurtful. Called out my work a failure during critique.
He didn't follow a project timeline at all. We were doing Pinterest vision boards for four weeks and then he suddenly remembered that we had to start on a semester project.

analysis.name: Allie Hirsch
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Allie could be teaching 'watching paint dry 101' and I would still take their course. They've always made me feel safe, respected, and valued as a student and encouraged me to pursue what I was passionate about. Classes were very well structured, and I was never confused about homework/lecture material. If you get the chance I highly recommend them

Allie is super kind and they are always open to talk, they gave help outside of class often and worked to create an inclusive and positive classroom environment! Grades in the course were fairly distributed with a heavy emphasis on participation so if you show up and complete every assignment on time you should get an A.

Was reflecting recently on my time in Alli's class. They showed me empathy and kindness that I did not receive from other profs at stamps. Alli has a special ability to tailor the assignments to the unique artist that each student is. I am very thankful for them.

Really lovely teacher and very accommodating and understanding. They really try to work with the students to make sure the class isn't too stressful but we still learn a lot. Allie also gives a lot of good feedback on each assignment, not just a grade. Grading criteria is clear and achievable.

Allie has to be my favorite professor at Stamps. They always make time for their students, and are always in an upbeat or understanding mood for classes. If you bring up a valid topic you think should be discussed in lecture, Allie will encourage you to follow up with it. When I was just coming into being queer, Allie told me about good resources

analysis.name: Guglielmo Audiberti
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is the best. Great best friend, always has suggestions to jump out the window. Tough, T-O-U-G-H grader. That il supposed to be la? 3 points off. Misspelled the word? kiss that A goodbye. Overall GUGU is hilarious and you will laugh and have fun in class but you must work hard to get a B . Also he will attack you with italian outside of class.

Easy class, workload is manageable. He reviews for exams in class. Most of class is speaking exercises, so you get a lot of practice with the language. He is a very fair grader, and tends to be very gracious when grading written and oral exams. Took him for two semester.

Hilarious and made learning a new language, which is so difficult, a lot of fun. He grades very fairly especially considering how common it was for students to make mistakes when reading/writing/speaking in a brand new language. If you have the choice to take Italian with any prof, it should be him, hands down the best prof I've had at all of UMich
Loved him so funny and I have learned so much italian. Best teacher I have had at Umich by far
He's only nice if he likes you.

analysis.name: Jonathan Brennan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Good prof, fun class! It really increased my interest in linguistics and cognitive science. The lectures were interesting and accessible (lecture recordings posted). I really appreciated the clear grading scheme and specifics about deadlines and late deadlines. The exams were also fairly easy + lowest one dropped. Overall, I recommend this class!

Condescending and paranoid about everyone using AI for some reason. Lectures were mandatory and boring yet there was no other way to learn besides rewatching lectures and trying to connect the dots on your own because GSIs were useless as well. Genuinely turned me away from an interest in linguistics.

Good professor, a lot of readings that aren't really necessary, lowest grades dropped. You do need to watch lectures though, and at times there can be too many examples shown. The class is fair, although your final grade is revealed toward the end which is also kind of annoying.

I didn't enjoy this class. It was pretty boring and not as fascinating as everyone makes it out to be. If you're into linguistics, this class is for you. If not, don't take it for elective credits, it's not worth the headaches and harsh grading.

I'm surprised at how low his ratings are! His lectures are different than the standard PowerPoint, but I did not find it difficult to adjust. I have had very little linguistics training, and I was able to keep up with linguistics majors. He has also been flexible and willing to help. Definitely would recommend Intro to Neurolinguistics overall

analysis.name: Alex Poniatowski
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 202 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: It is clear that Poniatowski knows a great deal about this subject, but often seems to forget that none of us have a degree in chemistry and rarely spends time explaining concepts. He also has random temper tantrums that are very distracting and condescending. He never cleans the chalkboards properly which is super annoying.

I've never seen a instructor who's five minutes late for almost all the lectures and office hours, making the concepts more confusing, and not willing to help students. Orgo isn't easy. If you want to learn something from the lectures instead of googling everything and learning it all by yourself at home, then don't take it with him!
i ended up just skipping his lecture and going to bartley's instead for the majority of the time. he's funny but is not good at teaching chem unfortunately

Dr. Poniatowski is very energetic and entertaining. However, he doesn't hit everything that needs to be covered for the course and can get sidetracked. I liked the way he explained things, but I had to start going to Bartley's lectures to get all of the information. My grade got a lot better when I switched. Overall very nice guy.

Although he's a good lecturer, the format in which he teaches the class is unnecessarily confusing and annoying to follow. He's a rude guy who doesn't seem to understand that students have many classes and puts in very little extra effort for the class past lectures. Hope he puts in effort in the future and makes handouts or anything for students.

analysis.name: Moulinath Banerjee
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: A masterful professor. I took his class some time ago, and I still reflect on it as one of my best college classes. I know a lot of people do not like him, but (I think) it is because the class isn't easy. That does not make him a poor teacher though. After all, I want U of M to be a place where the best students are challenged to work hard.

Mouli is actually knowledgeable and kind. However, he tried to teach us too many concepts, and was kind of disorganized. The intention was good though, and the concepts he taught were actually pretty interesting and shall be useful in statistical research. For first-time learners, it did take us efforts to reorganize and understand the whole story.

Lectures were kinda incoherent and lacking in structure; math was written on the board but there was no explanation of how it all tied together. Not much correlation between what was covered in class and on the exams/homework. Office hours changed every week, making it hard to get help.

The homework problems are well designed. However, completing the homework alone is not sufficient preparation for the exams. It is important to also spend time summarizing the key points from the corresponding textbook chapters. With sufficient effort, the outcome can be very good; without it, performance may suffer significantly.

Great professor. Highly knowledgable about theoretical statistics and offers great advice. He occasionally goes on tangents during lecture, but always comes across as warm and helpful. Relatively low-workload class if you pay attention in lecture, fairly methodic exams.

analysis.name: Greg Bodwin
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bodwin is such an amazing lecturer! Even though the class itself was rather difficult, he made lectures engaging and entertaining, and I looked forward to coming to class every single day. Even though attendance wasn't required, I still showed up to his lectures because he really is just that great of a teacher. 100% recommend for 203!

Bodwin is by FAR the best 203 lecturer. He's easy to listen to and on the 2x lecture recordings really sounds like Jesse Eisenberg! I didn't go in person to class so I tried all three lecturers and he stood out as the best. Take the advanced version of the class and the last 10 minutes is always a fun/weird puzzle. super interesting.

Phenomenal professor. Extremely passionate about his job and teaching the students. Very caring/respectful and quite witty, always in a super infectious good mood. Wish I had him for all my classes. Made some tough material easier to understand.

203 was the hardest class I have ever taken in my life. Homework was unnecessarily long and exam median grades were 60% before the curve (thank god there was a curve). However, Bodwin himself was a great professor (I watched his lectures) and he made learning the content feel fun at times, although it was a difficult class when I took it

Pros: 
- Great async lectures
- Good speaker, and answers questions well
- Writes a lot of the homework problems, so office hours are helpful

Cons:
- Writes the hardest discovery problems

analysis.name: Edwin Bergin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Loved this class. Three exams, all pretty difficult, but the weekly homework is simple and worth about half of your grade. Prof Bergin really loves what he's teaching and keeps lectures interesting. Definite recommendation if you have any interest in astronomy.

He is very passionate about this class which made lectures interesting. The IClicker questions were tough so you definitely had to be paying attention in class to get a good participation grade. Tests are not easy, but if you study a lot they are definitely manageable. Homework and quizzes are easy.

Lectures are sometimes a little boring, but the topic was fairly interesting. He's clearly passionate about the subject. If you read the textbook, this class is very easy. Amazing curve on all of the tests and grade cutoffs are great. Easy NS distribution.
Bergin was interesting in lectures but did go off on tangents and sometimes would randomly cancel class for conferences he had to attend, overall was a fairly easy interesting class for me though.
I loved this class and thought the lectures were engaging and understandable. The homework and tests were also not too difficult. I would definitely take a class with this professor again!

analysis.name: Elizabeth Houbeck
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I was very nervous going into Spanish due to the intensive language program at UMich, but Profesora Houbeck made it a wonderful experience. She is very patient and kind, and I highly recommend taking her if you have the opportunity.
Dr. Houbeck is a really kind, caring professor and always seems to enjoy teaching. She was amazing and I hope to take another class with her again at some point!

She was a great professor to have, I would definitely recommend her. She is not too strict about grading, and she does a great job teaching the language. I liked how she made the class very welcoming and relaxing.

You can tell that Professor Houbeck genuinely cares about her students and understands that all LSA students must fulfill this class. She never hesitated to help me and was one of the best Spanish teachers I have ever had!

Prof. Houbeck is a very nice, caring person. You can tell she was passionate about Spanish language and structure. She kind of assigns a lot of busy work, but honestly it really helped me for the midterms/final (especially the oral exam).

analysis.name: Barbara Koremenos
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Koremenos is more concerned with her own attendance numbers than the success of her students. She doesn't post powerpoints to the student site, and goes through them far too quickly in lecture, preventing students from taking complete notes and making studying difficult. Large portions of grades are determined by pop quizzes.

The amount of readings given for this class is inconceivable for a three-credit course. The first class she said that there won't always be readings, that is a lie. There are multiple readings every class. She says that there will occasionally be pop quizzes. Also a lie. They are every. single. class. Attendance is mandatory. 

Passive-aggressive.

Professor Koremenos was very frequently late in arriving to class, which is bewildering. When she did finally show up, she was repeatedly rude and condescending to students, especially to anyone who asked completely legitimate questions during class. She clearly did not want to be teaching. She should go find a different line of work.

This was the worst course I've EVER taken. She is extremely disorganized and unclear. At the end of the last class, she announced that we were going to have a final, even though the whole semester she claimed we should work harder because we WOULDN'T have a final. Nothing was ever graded in a timely manner, and was insanely hard for an intro class.

The structure of this class is vague, and I didn't learn much about world politics. She focused most of the class on two main group projects. One was related to world politics, and the second was on solar geoengineering- way too much time was spent on research that has little connection to world politics. She added an EXAM the LAST day of class.

analysis.name: Kathryn Babayan
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I took the class with the expectation that I would learn a lot about the build up to the conflict happening in the Middle East today. I didn't. Prof Babayan does not cover anything. She rambles on and on about the material, which she obviously knows, but students comprehend .25% of what she says. This class is not worth it.

Definitely a class to avoid. Brutal lectures that are near impossible to follow, you can't understand a word she says, and attendance is mandatory. I feel as though it could have been an interesting class with a different professor, but as it is her class isn't worth the trouble.

Eh. She seems like a nice lady, who certainly knows what she's talking about, but she can't teach for the life of her. She teaches history in a kind of "storybook" format, with little care for solid factual events. Personal bias is evident. Powerpoints consist entirely of pictures, which makes studying a bear. If you can find another prof, do it.

I read all of these reviews and I still took the class bc it fit perfectly into my schedule and I thought "how could the history of sexuality be boring? It'll still be interesting even if I don't love the professor." Don't be like me. Professor > Subject for electives ALWAYS. You never know what you might find interesting! Good prof never fails.

I did not enjoy this class at all. Professor Babayan's lectures seem to be one long tangent, and its difficult to discern what is important to know and what is just an aside. She had no clear grading criteria for assignments, and seemed to have unspoken/ unshared expectations for assignments.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Guilmet
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Guilmet can come across a bit intense initially but that's more a result of her sincerity regarding the course matter. She has high standards cause she really believes in her students. I am thankful to have had the opportunity to study under her. If you need extra support on projects she is available, understanding, and legitimately cares.

Apparently, Liz is great with first-year students and non-majors. Still, she must have been on a power trip when she got the opportunity to teach upper-level students because she was insufferable, controlling, and condescending. If you lack any creative ideas and want to be held and yanked around like a child, Liz is your perfect lecturer.

She comes off as intimidating and strict at first, but she's honestly super sweet. She forces you to step a bit out of your comfort zone with critiques where you stand alone in front of the class and present someone else's work, but she gives you candy and is super supportive. I loved all the conversations I had with her.
Is strict and uptight but overall cares about students a lot. Is really good at teaching.

I loved her. She does come off as judgey but in a good way. She gives very helpful feedback and actually teaches! I love her teaching style and how instead of lecturing she actually has us do exercises and she also lets students have creative freedom instead of strict guidelines. I HIGHLY recommend taking her at least once during your time here

analysis.name: Steven Clark
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 132 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He taught the course for the second half, and I really think 90% of the people in the class have no recollection of what he taught. He runs through huge concepts and honestly makes no sense. The average on his exam was a 68! A 68! Unheard of in an intro class. Just to top it all off, he didn't get an ovation on the last day of class. Avoid. AVOID.

If you're an AP/Transfer starting at UM-AA on the fence about taking this class: know Prof. Clark is patient, passionate, very accessible, and truly an expert; his smaller class size makes iClicker, Study Groups, and Discussions easy points just for showing up—also allows for a personal connection. I honestly dont know anyone who regrets taking it!

Clark's good during lecture! He's much less monotone than people claim. It's outside of lecture where I have a problem. He's very rude to students asking concept questions on piazza. He'll answer with things like "that's a good question" and "rewatch the last three lectures." He's very unapproachable during office hours. And, his exams are harder.

Dr. Clark only teaches the 2nd half of the semester for this course, but he is WAY BETTER than Clowney! I wish he taught it the whole semester. He tends to go through slides quick, but he explains the concepts well and puts emphasis on the right things. Exams in the second half of the semester after he took over were easier and ran more smoothly.

Genuinely one of my favorite professors. He explained content really well and was passionate. His exams were usually accurate to the lectures. I also liked the way discussion was structured to not be overwhelming. He also gave a good amount of extra credit. Overall, as long as you understand the content (not just memorize), you'll be all good.

analysis.name: David BARTLEY
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 247 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Oh Bartley, where do I even begin. Never in my 18 years of life have I encountered an exam so utterly ridiculous that I stopped praying for a good grade on the exam and began praying for a bomb to land near me so I never have to see something so sinister ever again. Also—thanks for your completely unhelpful and apathetic copy-paste Piazza comments.
Bartley???? More like BARKLEY!!!! ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF ARFF

Great lecturer, and office hours with Bartley can be helpful/interesting. However, all of the exams are much more difficult than any practice exam material given. Like its majority free response and the questions are written to trick you. I'd highly recommend signing up for a SLC study group, and focus on studying applications not just concepts.

Bartley has single-handedly taken an entire 100-level class to the shadow realm. His exams are far harder than practice exams and often don't match the format/difficulty. We even had a question from an un-lectured section (confirmed by the GSI). TAKE THIS CLASS ONLY IF YOU MUST, and if you do buckle up, this ain't 2024 chem 130 no more.

Dr. Bartley is a good lecturer, however his communication with students has been immature and unprofessional. While providing students with an easy exam is not required, properly informing them about what to expect is. Personally, I did well in his class, but no amount of review could have prepared anyone for content that was not clearly explained.

analysis.name: Carla Iglesias-Garrido
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 59 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely loved this class and learned so much, decent amount of work but it was manageable and I feel like my Spanish was at it's best while in this class. We spoke so much Spanish in class every day which really helped me. Carla wanted the best for us so held us to high standards but was super understanding when things came up, 100% recommend!

DO NOT take 232 with Carla. I can't even fathom how she has gotten such good reviews in the past (which is what made me take the class with her, a decision I greatly regret). Very condescending and acts like she cares about students, gets involved in their personal life. Made me hate taking the language. Unless you are fluent, don't take with her!!

Whatever you do, please avoid taking Spanish 232 with Carla for your own sanity! When you go to her office hours, she will watch you struggle repeatedly without offering any assistance. She watched me cry for help physically and metaphorically and laughed in my face, like actually. I also wrote this in my evaluations, yet nothing changed.

Although I am aware that 232 is a weeder class and is meant to be challenging, other weeder classes have 1) excellent instructors. 2) Teachers who are aware that their course is challenging yet go above and beyond to ensure you grasp the material. Carla didn't do either. For no apparent reason, she made her lesson more difficult.

I can assure you that every one of the thirty or so people who are currently praising this class as "awesome" are either fluent in spanish or white (probably both). Not even trying to go there, but Carla's microaggression is crazy. Really, girl, in 2025? Uncomfortable surroundings, awful atmosphere, and a terrible teacher.

analysis.name: Chris Schad
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is AMAZING! So kind, respectful, and funny. Class is difficult, but if you pay attention and try your best it is worth it. He is absolutely a must have if you are taking Japanese. I never thought I was wasting my time in his class. Also, his schedule for the course is very detailed and clear, no confusion there. 10/10 professor!

Amazing! I had him in 2020-21 for both fall and winter semesters. Schad-sensei is a great lecturer and makes Japanese learning so easy and fun. He is also very quick to respond to emails and was very helpful with questions about grammar. I wish he taught other Japanese language courses; as I go into 300 level, I miss 
his positive energy.

He is the best teacher I have ever had. He is so funny and he is respectful, understanding, and explains everything so well. I had him for all of Japanese 1 and 2. It is clear that he has a passion for helping students learn Japanese
Amazing teacher. He is more than willing to help you with any problems you are having. Just make sure to participate in class and never hesitate to ask questions.
He's very affable, and his office hours are super helpful. I recommend his classes for students that want a challenge but also want a welcoming environment.

analysis.name: Charlie O'Geen
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I would never take his class willingly. He does not teach but rather switches ideas from class to class in order to assert his dominance over the students. He answers questions with an attitude. Takes attendance at an arbitrary time, and if you are not in the classroom space within that time (ex. bathroom, printing...) he will mark you as absent.

Bad instructor for an interdisciplinary course. Taubman Architecture department students are advised by academic advisors not to take his classes. He creates a harsh environment and does not allow for any small mistakes on assignments even with unclear instructions. Very mean when asked a question.

ahn is by far an amazing prof, makes stats interesting with fun pop culture references and is just a cool, jolly guy

I highly recommend it!

Professor Adunbi is extremely knowledgeable in his subject area. review_highlights.comment: This class was very challenging, and I often felt unsupported when asking questions. Responses were harsh and focused on the curve, which made it difficult to seek help and left me more confused rather than clarified.

Very monotone. Never started class with "hello how are you?" and didn't look to make a personal connection. She wasn't very sympathetic when answering questions. Overall, the class was kind of interesting, and she was very obviously smart. The long classes were pretty miserable and I never once looked forward to class,

It will be by far the most difficult BBA class to date. She did a good job of cracking jokes to lighten the mood; however, it is such a long and boring lecture and its so easy to only start caring about the midterm and final right before. Midterm and final are your entire grades and depending on your section the average could be below a 70 or 85+.

Not a tough class neccesairly, just something that catches BBAs off guard.

Best gameplan for this class:
1. slides before class for 30 mins (use AI to help you get general feeling for content)
2. pay attention in class (try and participate at least once but otherwise just listen)
3. try and rewatch lectures after class
4. do hw (actually do it!)

TO301 is going to be a difficult class regardless of who you have as your professor. I felt that Prof. Astashkina explained material clearly but since the class is fast-paced, I had to rewatch lectures and go over my notes for things I missed. As long as you put effort into this class, you will be fine.

analysis.name: Asaf Cohen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Very clear lectures and homework solutions. Exams are similar to practice exams and homework. Extremely dedicated to students (his two gsi's were told to hold extra weekly tutoring sessions to do practice problems). The best part is that u don't need to take the class synchronously. I only watched the recorded lectures.

Great professor and great lectures. Everything is very organized. I liked rewatching lecture recordings. Homework takes a long time, but office hours are helpful. Exam difficulty was fair, and the grades are curved. Prof. Cohen has a good sense of humor and gives intuitive examples. Great addition to the math department.

Lecture notes are constructed from scratch and straightforward to read. Both lecture notes and HWs are super helpful for exams. Skiped all classes and learned all the things from lecture notes over the final week and got an A+. Frankly speaking, Math 423 is one of the easiest math courses at UofM, and Asaf is definitely the best among all sections.

He always provides intuition for what we're learning and avoids overcomplicating the topics. Everything is recorded, so you can always go back to rewatch lectures. There are no surprises on the exams (though there might be a couple difficult parts), and he grades fairly. Definitely one of my favorite math classes.

The materials being discussed in math 474 are really helpful in the sense that they give a rather comprehensive framework of mathematical finance beyond the more "toy" model we've seen in math 423. Asaf is a great lecturer. He pays lots of attention to intuition and clarifies many things in the textbook.

analysis.name: Adam Ashforth
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Professor Ashforth is a phenomenal professor. He is incredibly knowledgeable and wise, and has great insights into Africa, as well as its context in global health. If you don't like to do your work, participate, actually think and use your brain, and write - then don't take this class. For everyone else, this is an exceptional seminar class!

50% of your grade is a 20-page research paper graded based on "best effort, however "best effort" isn't defined. The expectations were unclear and there were minimal discussions surrounding the paper. He claims he's gonna teach you how to write a research paper, but he doesn't. This isn't a discussion-based class, he lectures the entire time.

Adam did not make the classroom feel like a comfortable place, but attendance was mandatory. Also only grade was 15 page paper that we had very little instruction on. Do not recommend him at all, worst class ever.

Finished today my last lecture in Professor Ashforth's AAS 326 class and he is an amazing man. Funny, witty, intelligent, sarcastic, and just an extremely down to earth guy. The class was small and discussion based on different topics that we were able to choose from. 1 research paper and 2-3 small in class assignments was the workload! Great guy!

Dude is an absolute authority in his field, and hilarious in class. The whole "one paper per semester" thing is perfectly reasonable if you know what you're signing up for--you spend the entire class preparing for it, and he tells you it's the case right from the get-go. Definitely a tough grader, but by no means unreasonable.  Highly recommend.

Her lectures are crystal clear and exams are just more lengthy homework on time limit. Try to go to review class before the exam since she gives hints and explains common mistakes students make.

Good teacher. Very clear on expectations for overall class. Have to take advantage of all the resources she offers. Covers a lot of material so staying on top of discussions, homeworks, and practice problems will prepare you well for exams as she doesnt throw you many curveballs.
Good professor. Pretty easy exams!

Great professor. She's great at explaining it clearly and making her expectations clear. She'll stop the whole class and go over material if a student doesn't understand it. Her classes are extremely helpful to go to and her exams reflect what she teaches. would recommend.

Ashley is one of the best professors I've had at the university.  She can easily relate to her students and I find myself actually excited to attend lecture.  Tests aren't difficult as long as you read and come to lecture.

Professor Gearhardt was super enthusiastic and knowledgeable on the topic of abnormal psych! There are iClicker questions in lecture so attendance is mandatory. Always go to section. analysis.name: Austin Yarger
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly

review_highlights.comment: Austin is one of the most impressive instructors I've had. Not only is he unquestionably knowledgeable on every topic he teaches, but his genuine care and effort that he invests in the class is unlike most other professors at the university. His lectures are some of the most engaging you'll have, and though the class is a challenge, it's worth it.

Austin lives and breathes game development and it shows. Over the course of the class, he really pushes you to make a game that is interesting, polished, and fun. It's a lot of work but it's a really fun process and it's the kind of thing you want to work on. He's a caring guy, very invested in making the class great and the students successful.

His lectures are easy to understand and fun, but sometimes arent immediately useful for projects. He suffers from DKC music addiction and doesnt seem to sleep very much either. You probably won't either, but you can look forward to learning alot about game dev. RIP hair.

Professor Yarger is an amazing teacher. He gives a lot of career advice and resources, while also creating interactive and fun lecture environments that teach important concepts. 494 has a pretty intense workload, but all the feedback from assignments and guidance during office hours is really helpful and pushes you in the right direction.

Austin genuinely wants his students to succeed and do well in his classes. He not only offers thoughtful advice on the your games but also provides opportunities for extra credit. His lectures are informative, showcasing different games and their mechanics that influence player decisions. The concepts he presents are helpful for your final game.

I took her pilot class and I didn't enjoy it as much as I thought I would, but she was fine. Personally, I don't get along well with her teaching style, but I think overall she's a passionate and great professor.

I've never met anyone with more knowledge of Early Modern drama than Audrey Becker. Her passion for the topic shows and she finds different ways for everyone to connect with the material. review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. No tech, but in class notes don't really help since the midterm + final + essays were based on terms in his study guide (remember ~200 terms per exam).

analysis.name: Ayyalusamy Ramamoorthy

Clearer communication and respect for schedules would have greatly improved the class.

Lectures make sense after you review the material in the book.  He loves to breeze through derivations, don't get hung up on them, just understand the concepts behind them. Rams is one of the hardest working and most knowledgeable professors in Chemistry and Biophysics at Michigan. He consistently treats his students with the respect of an equal ? a very admirable quality. He is extremely approachable, caring, and supportive of his students ? always willing to give guidance when/where needed; he is a natural teacher.

Very useful class.  Rams really cared about the quality of our submitted work, gave us a lot of resources to do well, was really really helpful to the students who wanted to go the extra-mile, was always flexible.. all around great professor and class.

Very unpredictable and lazy. His tests aren't supposed to be that hard but sometimes he gives these unexpected questions with a lot of points that people get right for guessing right. So because he is unpredictable he is either very hard or easy depending on how well you catch on with the prof's teaching method and type of exam problems.

analysis.name: Ayaka Sogabe

Sogabe sensei is wonderful and has really helped me better understand the material being taught. She's very engaging in her lectures and keeps the mood of the class fun and lighthearted. Be prepared to participate and speak fully in Japanese. It's difficult at first but it really helps you improve your speaking skills.

Sogabe sensei is all-around a great teacher. She's very engaging during her lectures, always open to questions, and conveys the material clearly. Be prepared to participate and speak entirely in Japanese. It's difficult at first but it really helps your speaking skills to develop.

Sogabe-sensei was great despite there being mandatory attendance, lots of hw and forced participation. This forced me to not be lazy and I truly believe this heavier handed approach bodes well for those who genuinely want to learn japanese. No cake walk but given how different the language is from english the class always felt do-able.

I've had nothing but good experiences with Sogabe-sensei. Expect to participate, speak only in Japanese, and come to class prepared, but these all help to improve your language abilities tremendously. She's very funny and keeps class engaging with her enthusiasm. On assignments, she gives great feedback and is fair in grading.

Awful professor, didn't even care if the class learned anything, just burping numbers on the board. Group projects were a disaster, no grading criteria, nor explanation. Usual professor that makes exams with things he didn't teach, always arguing with students. As a pro now I realize that most of his material was useless for real pro life.

Goker does a great job explaining the Production and Supply Chain material.  He does a great job of picking out the important stuff from the chapters and simplifying it. Always ready to go out of his way to help students even in class...and sometimes ends up not having enough time to do all what he wanted in a lecture. Very available. Exams and howework are challenging and long so beware. Overall a good professor.
Great prof.  I recommend highly!

analysis.name: Sarah  Azmeh

Best professor at UM, very kind and understanding and the topics covered in class were very interesting!!  Highly Recommend!!!!!
Very nice lecturer, super generous grading. It would be even better if attendance is not mandatory. Still highly recommended.

analysis.name: Catherine Barry

review_highlights.comment: I love Cathy Barry! I had her for drawing observation (option wasn't available in the drop down menu) and absolutely adored the class. She is very kind and her classes were always engaging and useful. Get ready to do a lot of nature drawing!

Cathy is very sweet and very helpful. She is also fairly flexible on syllabus, I reflected my interest in painting outdoors for sceneries and she had adapted the syllabus based on students' suggestions. She gives useful feedback along the way and is very sweet. She encourages students of different levels to paint.

I am writing about Cathy as an Art & Design History discussion leader. She is very nice and caring. I managed to receive all 4/4 on my discussion posts, never got a bonus pts tho (might just be me). She will get visibly upset if no one speaks up, but she won't force you to speak if you don't raise your hand. She's probably the best discussion lead

Cathy is a wonderful art teacher. This is the first time I learned how to paint with watercolor and I will continue it for a lifetime. She teaches well, gives good feedback. There is hw due every Thurs. Cathy is kind and inspirational and I am thankful for that! You will have to buy art supplies though b/c the course fee does not cover everything.
She's a nice person. Her grading is fair. You should be glad if you have her.

analysis.name: Aynur Bulut

review_highlights.comment: TERRIBLE! I learned more while teaching myself from the book than ever I did in class. She teaches in the least common-sense way and forces people to participate in a big lecture. If they answer questions incorrectly she is condescending and says "this is easy" or "you should know this". She has an accent but in my opinion it wasn't too bad.

She was a lot better than people give her credit for. She meant well and wanted students to learn. She always wanted students to participate to show that they were keeping up with the material. Also, the test averages for her classes were higher than for the other sections with different teachers.

A very unhelpful instructor. She frequently claims that “this is so simple” even though she constantly make computational errors. She does not explain examples on new topics and is very hard to follow her work (a 9 looks like a g, while a g looks like a p in her writing). Worst teacher I have ever had.  She frequently insults students and complains when students (involuntarily) are forced to help and are wrong.  Thick accent.  Lectures are verbatim from the book and she still make mistakes computationally.  When she is wrong, she looks at her notes and says that the student is wrong without considering.  Avoid!

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR IF AT ALL POSSIBLE! Her lectures are unhelpful and often confusing. Rather than answering questions, she just tells you that "it's easy" and "you should know this" (even if it's completely new material). She has a thick accent, so it is often hard to understand her. Do yourself a favor and avoid her.

analysis.name: Megan Bardolph

Grading is mostly weighted by 2 essays (with revisions) plus attendance. P.S. you may learn to juggle!

Professor Bardolph is genuinely one of the best professors that the school has to offer. She takes a seemingly mundane and boring class (ENG125), and adds so much complexity and thought into how to develop our rhetoric to gain a better understanding of writing and academic inquiry. Also an extremely sweet lady and clearly cares for her students!

Dr. Bardolph is amazing! She made the lectures interesting and enjoyable. I really enjoyed my time in her class and the things we discussed have helped me a lot. She is very friendly and always willing to talk about literally anything!

Prof Bardolph is so sweet and cares so much about the well-being of her students! She barely gave any work outside of class. The class was not super helpful in improving English skills and focused more on rhetoric which is not what I had expected, but she made it pretty enjoyable. Class is very very easy and not much is missed if you skip lecture.

Very light workload and engaging lectures made her class the highlight of otherwise tough days for me. She assigns work qualitatively with succinct but thoughtful guidelines I found nice. Hands down the perfect FYWR class you could take.

analysis.name: Basil Dufallo

review_highlights.comment: Prof Dufallo's lectures had nothing to do with our essays. Professor Dufallo's class was extremely interesting and he is so knowledgeable. I have no idea why people seemed to miss lecture a lot but they missed out on some great lectures. I would highly recommend this course. It was not super difficult and I learned so much.

His lectures just had nothing to do with our essay prompts, which was our entire class grade and also incredibly difficult and unorganized. A different teacher came and taught for a week and she was much better than him. Would be a good class otherwise.

Professor Dufallo is a great classics professor, but as a first year writing course his lectures often become misguided regarding the essay prompts. Grade depends on GSI. Strict technology policies and he also as a rather strict AI policy, as a bunch of kids this semester were accused of using AI falsely.

analysis.name: Lesa Begley

Overall, excellent professor and class.
Wish I knew why I was honor coded :(. Makes no sense to hand it out when students don't know why and trouble their lives for it to prove they're right and still lose.

This professor wasn't very accessible via the duration of the course despite wielding substantial stakes over final course grades. It's as if potential communication opportunities with them was purposefully limited on their end.
ENGR 101 professors are incredibly committed to their student's success.

The professor works really hard. But I thought the lecture was a little out-of-date. Some code style and functionality is useless during actual work. He should provide more useful stuff in this course, or it will just be a waste of time

This was one of the most toughest classes because I don't have a CS background. He is very helpful outside of class but office hours were limited to only Fridays for a few hours. GSI was also helpful but you may need to study a lot outside of class. He does rush through the lecture but does have recorded lectures. Work hard and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Geoffrey Bankowski
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

He has high expectations for his students, and it can come off as a lot at first. However, he's genuinely one of the most understanding professors I've had here. If you put in the work by doing the readings and communicating, he'll give you a good grade.

Professor Bankowski is an ok professor. He seems more fun and interactive than he actually is. He assigns so many readings that are very long and convoluted, and expects you to finish them before all the classes. Spends lots of time lecturing and papers get decent feedback. Nice person to interact with.

By far the worst professor I've ever encountered at UMICH. Truly on an ego-high and continuously disrespected and belittled classmates of mine in this course. A "B" is not too difficult, but anything higher will require imagination, skill, effort. Feedback from papers and office hours did not help me. analysis.name: Bethany Kreps
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly

I haven't even finished the class yet, but she's definitely my best teacher this semester and probably this year. Super kind, very flexible, caring, and understanding. As long as you try, you'll definitely get a good grade.

I really liked Madame Kreps. I hated French in High School, but I enjoyed this class. I hate participating in class and participation was a part of our grade so I was nervous going in, but she made me feel really comfortable and the class is small so it's not that bad. She was a pretty nice grader and gave us a lot of feedback on our work.

Professor Kreps was an extremely kind and understanding professor! She was easy to understand and very approachable, so oral exams and asking questions weren't as scary as I thought they would be. Participation wasn't as difficult as I expected either since the class was small and Professor Kreps made the environment comfortable.

I would highly recommend people take Mme. Kreps classes! She was one of my favorite profs here so far, she kept the class stress-free, and I never felt nervous to participate or afraid to make mistakes. She's very kind and if you participate in class you should do really well

analysis.name: Benjamin Hollenbach

analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 82 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Hollenbach is so goated. His lectures are very fun and entertaining while also informative. Attendance isn't required for lecture, but it is for section. Your grade is based off 3 exams, 2 writing assignments, and section attendance. Very easy class with practically no work. Exams are very easy and so are the writing assignments.

This guy is the goat. While I hate to admit I almost never showed up to lecture, I'd watch the lecture videos in my dorm and he made me laugh a couple times. Really energetic and the topics were decently interesting. Exams aren't too hard, but the released study guides are helpful and cover everything. Had cool selfies too and loved Ariana Grande

Prof Hollenbach was passionate about his studies and made them really interesting for us. He often connected his lectures to pop culture references, making them really enjoyable. Tests were straightforward if you studied the study guide. The only thing is that at times it was unclear exactly what we were to do for the writing assignments.

I, like most others, didn't attend lectures but would rewatch them for upcoming exams and was genuinely so entertained. He used a lot of pop-culture references making the content more bearable, and the exams were extremely fair. He's also very willing to accommodate exam changes and just great to talk to. Would honestly recommend to anyone

He is the best professor I've had so far!! He made seemingly boring topics so interesting, and I always looked forward to the lectures. Lecture's aren't mandatory, but you are missing out so much by watching the recorded lectures. He genuinely wants all of his students to succeed. The expectation for the writing assignments and exams are clear.

By far the best professor I've ever encountered and universally recognized as one of the best researchers in the field.  His book is also fantastic.

Would argue material in discussion with the GSI, no coherence there.  Exams were very easy, open book but not an enjoyable class or one that I learned anything in.

Great professor and super funny. Really cares about students truly learning and understanding the material. Homeworks were pretty hard and the midterm was rough. But he made the final very easy. I was one of the dumbest in the class and ended up with a decent grade, so I imagine the smart kids all got easy A's. Good class to take.

My 320 experience: lectures 1-5: no idea what is going on finally read textbook, realize its not the difficult. First Midterm - analytical, basic, like HW Final - Conceptual, if you paid some attention in class you'll be fine Overall: I was often lost during lecture, but doing HW and occasionally reading led me to an A

analysis.name: Varuni Bhatia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Varuni Bhatia was a wonderful professor. She actually engaged everyone with the material, brought a lot of viewpoints into discussion (and the entire class was essentially discussing the readings) and your grade is almost certainly an A if you try on the presentation and the two papers. Wonderful class, wonderful prof, would take again.

She is very straightforward and an overall sweet lady; however, the grading in her class is unfair. The highest grade you are allowed to obtain is a 95% on all assignments, including participation and attendance, even if you attended every lecture, and you need a 95% or above to get an A. Most people get an A minus, but an A is not obtainable.

Asian 336 with Prof. Bhatia is fun. She brings in many aspects relating to the topic and has great interaction with class. Beware, She expects you to read a lot! The articles she brings to class are unique and help clearly understand the topic. Her grading is a little strict but she guides you on how to write complete and good papers.

VB is super sweet and enthusiastic about the material. The midterm was easy because she provided a study guide, but the final exam ended up being really difficult. We had to learn a lot of the material for the final from the textbook by ourselves. But overall, I learned a lot from this class and I would recommend it to others.

Prof. Bhatia was very clear in her expectations of the class, and the coursework was very manageable. Class participation is a major part of the grade, but you can "contribute" in a number of ways. Very thorough in the different modules. Class was kind of dull sometimes, but overall I'm glad I took it.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Buvinger

Probably the worst professor I have ever had. She reads word for word off her slides. Exams have extremely specific information from readings. GSIs are nice, luckily. Just avoid any class with her.
Only teaches by reading off of her slides and showing videos. Stuffs too much information onto tests and tests are too hard.

Expects you to memorize multiple chapters of two textbooks and asks extremely specific questions on exams. Discussion was not helpful, and neither were lectures. Too much studying was expected for an intro course, do not take a class with this woman.

Dr. Buvinger is very engaging and accomodating for office hours.The only issue I had was it was difficult to know what to actually study and have written down for the weekly quizzes because the content we had to read and the content we got from lecture was very broad. I recommend taking notes on the readings and participating often in discussions.

he mumbles during class the entire time and when people participate he will tell them to speak up and use their Ross voices if they are not as loud

Pray you have a good IA, his office hours are worthless... and so are the lectures.

Decent professor. I didn't go to lectures because he often went off topic and on long tangents. But he one of the most understanding and caring professors I've had so far. If you completed the last take home exam late, he would still take it. Overall a good professor in terms of understanding but an okay teacher.

Sharqi is super accessible and tries his best to teach the breadth of material, which there's a lot since it is an overview of some of the math and science concepts used. He is kind and understanding though.

The class is expected to be easy because it is an introductory class, but it seems it's not. For exam 2, I was halfway through, and I am sure half of the class didn't finish the exam. Homework is also longggg..

Consider self learning as the professor does not teach content relevant to homework and exams very well. 
Understanding content is easier with practice exam keys instead of attending exam review sessions as he will make errors.
Never expect to finish any of his exams as in the allotted time.
The exams look nothing like lecture slide material.

analysis.name: Bradley Biggs
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining

In the lectures, the professor failed to define many variables and lacked any flow in his line of thought.  Not great at simplifying conceptual explanations. Homework was very helpful until it stopped relating to lecture content. Homework had long simulation problems that took hours to learn and then implement.

analysis.name: Michele Bird

She's honestly pretty blunt and can come across rude which makes her hard to approach at times. You have to get above a 60% on each exam to earn credit, which can be extremely defeating. Definitely a class that requires so much effort.

First off, part of the issue with my grade was that I wasn't as locked in as I should've been the semester I took this course. But, there is no reason to end lecture short by 20-30 minutes every class and just rush through the lecture and not explain things deeply. She is also a little curt, and not the friendliest (by her own admittance).

Feeling discouraged because, according to the recent exam statistics, about 1/3 of the class got less than a 60% on the most recent exam, which I woulldn't normally think is something crazy but if you get less than 60%, you get 0 points, even if you're like me, who got a 55% after lots of study. Good prof. but get ready to not get credit for effort

Dr. Bird was a great professor and knows makes lectures fun because of how much knowledge she has on all the content. Gradecraft class so you get to pick what assignments you do. There are 6 exams but as long as you get above a 60% on all of them and attend every class you can get an A+.

analysis.name: Julie Biteen

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Biteen is a great professor. She is clearly very passionate about what she's teaching, and she makes pchem concepts much more digestible and easier to understand. Biteen is the best! She structures her lectures and the discussions so well, you cannot help but do great! She is really funny and really loves her students. Could not recommend her more highly!

She's new to U of M, but she seems to know her stuff. She goes through the basic chem slides all the other teachers go through as well. She was very nice and is willing to answer questions. iClicker attendance is recommended since they can give you an extra 4% boost in the class. Exams are actually pretty  hard though since she doesn't write them.

Very sweet and caring. She goes at a pretty reasonable pace and is very open to helping people with questions so the lectures and iClickers were fairly easy for me (I had some previous experience with chem honors in high school). The tests are a little challenging though and aren't curved.

She's kind and will answer all of your questions. She occasionally makes no sense and often confuses her words, but if you point it out or go to her office hours, she clarifies. Very sweet and caring, makes cute little jokes here and there.

analysis.name: Bing Zhou
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

Your grade will thank you.

Worst class I have ever taken by far, 100% sure that any grad student would've done better. She read straight off slides for lecture, which were just screenshots from the solution manual. Only 5 people out of 30 were attending lecture after the first month, and every time you asked a question in office hours she would berate you. umich pls fire.

Professor Zhou was truly one of the worst professors that I have had at this school.  She expects everything to make sense the first time around and is very condescending in her explanations.  I was a solid A- average honors physics student going into this class, but completely bombed this course.  Definitely avoid her and try to get someone else.

Bing Zhou is very smart, but not a good lecturer. Her lectures skip over parts that would help student understanding and are scattered. She almost always does not understand students questions and makes mistakes when writing equations that often lead to confusing notes. Read the book, and good luck. If you can, wait for someone else to teach it.

The lectures are just Professor Zhou reading off a slideshow that they opened on Canvas. The homeworks are just book problems. She never walks through problems on a white/blackboard, only talks through them on the slides. I would never take a class with this professor again.

analysis.name: Bill Gehring
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 81 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I absolutely loved Dr. Gehring and his genuine care for each and every student. The interesting material covered in lecture was underscored by his passion for the subject. Exams are fair if you pay attention in lecture and review the study guide. I highly recommend 240 but take any class you can with Dr. Gehring, you won't regret it.

Bill was a great professor during the summer semester. He truly cared for his students and you could tell it too. I wasn't the best student due mental health issues, Bill was willing to take actions to get you where you should be. I've never had a more awesome professor at my time here in Michigan.

Bill Gehring is an amazing professor who clearly cares about the course and students. Only thing I will say is that the demos in class do come in the exam so participate and don't brush them off. Exams do require a lot of studying but aren't impossible. He also encourages AI and includes assignments that teach us about it. Great for BS credit.

He is so sweet and is such a good lecturer. He makes the content understable, even when it can be confusing like parts of the brain. The exams are really straightforward and he does curve them to help everyone out. He wants to get to know you so I recommend office hours or at least emailing him, he wants to hear from you!

Gehring is THE BEST PROFESSOR IVE HAD at uofm! His psych 240 taught me how to actually study and I learned so much in the class despite it being online and fast paced spring semester! He's an amazing lecturer, easy professor, and an amazing human. Its easy to do well in the class and to enjoy learning the material without dying of stress.

analysis.name: David Blaauw
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: the average for the exam was a 45 and there was 0 circuits involved it was all random fun fact questions on circuits and it was nothing like the TWOOOOO practice questions released like why are we getting set up for failure. why are there 0 good learning materials?

Blaauw is very knowledgeable and a good professor, but the organization + administrative aspects of his courses make it difficult to recommend. He only taught during the final ~4 weeks of the semester. The class was primarily led by GSIs who did their best. Additionally, his exams are extremely difficult, with class averages often below 50%.
Labs are incoherent and completely different from lectures and exam content is NOWHERE to be found it just appears on the exam somehow
Why does the exams have word for word questions from some random fabrication process mentioned for 2 seconds in lecture 1?
The Gsis ran the class he disappeared after day 1 unfortunately otherwise he wouldve been a great teacher :(.

analysis.name: Elliot Blackstone
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Waited until I graduated to make this judgement: Officially THE WORST Professor I have had.Simply put: Unwilling and unable to help one improve, unclear grading, memorization-based learning, dismissive, purely exam-based course grade, homework dissimilar to exams, does not explain concepts rather write definitions on board. Doesn't belong at UMich.

Prof Elliot only writing what is on the book during the lecture. It feels like there is nothing different between learning by yourself at home and listening the lecture. Anyways, the teaching skills is just awful.

Lectures were copied straight from the textbook, but example problems only covered the basics of the topics. Harsh grader on exams, and had poor explanations for grading. Explanations in class were vague, and I understood concepts better after teaching myself them.

Dr. Blackstone was a great professor—he explained everything clearly, graded fairly, and was always there to help with questions. He is sometimes a little bit blunt, but it's kind of funny. Great professor but not an easy class.

Fell far below the general standard of honors math. All exams (80% of our grade!) regurgitated problems from the textbook; studying became memorizing 100+ problems rather than LEARNING & ENJOYING math. Lectures copied from textbook. I started doing SO MUCH better (D -> A) once I started teaching myself from the textbook instead of going to class.

analysis.name: Hoyt Bleakley
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: For first few months of the semester, he had a high expectation from upper-level students so he explained the concept with extra details. This obviously confused the students but he simplified things at the end. I went to his office hour every week and got help for the problem set and understanding the concept. Exams are similar to problem sets.

I would genuinely never take 461. Ever. Actively googling "how to late drop a class". All written on a chalkboard. Very disorganized flow of ideas. Unsure of expectations. Lecture recordings are recorded but not made public because why would he make resources available to his students? Must request recordings when absent. No late homework allowed.

This guy is a nice person and all, he does care about the students and tries to give feedback if you ask for it. HOWEVER getting any type of straight answer out of him is like pulling teeth. I have to ask him the same question at least 2 times to get a clear response. Some of the content is really confusing, and he doesn't do his best to help you.

He doesn't seem to prepare for lecture and mandates a lot of assumed knowledge that is closer to a graduate level than undergraduate. If you are not excellent at the modeling side of economics avoid his course.

This class is confusing. He doesn't post lectures or slides online or in an organized manner. His lectures are unclear and uninteresting. Attendance isn't required, but most of the lecture is just him writing on the board, so you won't know what he talked about if you miss class. He's unclear about grading and expectations. Kind of pointless class.

analysis.name: Joel Blum
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Easy, especially if you go to lecture and pay attention. Discussion activities are easy and can be done at home and turned in later (aka lab attendance is optional). Gives you all questions prior to exam. Interesting lecturer, great teacher!

Professor seems like a kind person, but lectures were pretty boring. The weekly quizzes weren't exactly tough but pays attention to minor details, some that are even irrelevant. Overall, class wasn't hard since there were no exmas.

Joel is a wonderful teacher. He spells out exactly what you need to know for the test on his lecture slides, and it is quite possible to get a great score on the test without reading the text because of the thoroughness of the lecture (still, the book was fun). Very accessible teacher and loves his work. Strongly recommended teacher and fun class.

Professor Blum has a lot of interesting career experience and passion to share. However, the restructuring of this course didn't work for me, personally. I would attend lectures but still do poorly on the weekly quizzes. With last-minute extra credit I got an A+, but feel I learned very little. Not the best intro to a really cool subject matter.

This class was fine. There was little direction, though. Lecture heavy with lots of group paper reading and presenting on it. Other than that, thee class is graded on an exam and a paper. Very knowledgable but the class was confusing.

analysis.name: Anthony Bloch
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very good professor and course! The course uses ODE and geometric point of views to explain a lot of mechanical and physics phenomenon. The professor is very nice and always prepared. Office hours helps a lot for those who do not know much before. I learnt a lot even without taking much courses in analysis and geometry. Very inspiring overall.

Bloch had very useful office hours and would help explain the written homework, review questions, or recently learned concepts. Class was not always helpful, so go to office hours if you don't understand him. The book was often just as helpful as he was with general concepts. He sounds like Nigel Thornberry from "The WIld Thornberrys."

He's a nice guy but just a really bad lecturer. Exams and homeworks are not hard, but he fails to explain even the basic concepts in class and you don't know what he's even talking about most of the time, the only good thing about the class is the book, which he did a good job choosing for the class

Bloch is the man. During Calc 3, I hated it but now looking back it was actually a really great class, I always liked Bloch he's pretty good at teaching and is helpful, if you're going to take applied honors Cal 3 definitely take it with him

Professor Bloch is a great guy that challenges you in the hw assignments, but grades leniently and give fair exams. His lectures are very interesting and he has a very subtle humor. One of my favorite classes.

analysis.name: Julio Blanco
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Blanco was completely unorganized. There was no clear grading scheme and he made the test extremely hard. The hw questions he assigned were useless in helping to understand the material for the test. He was a very tough grader despite the already hard test. He also has a very strong accent and cannot explain class material clearly. The worst!!

I was really excited to take this class as I thought it was an interesting topic. However, I had a very hard time understanding him because of his thick accent. Even his writing was unclear at times. The class was all exams that were heavily weighted towards multiple choice. He was willing to hear student concerns and accessible outside of class.

He pre-records videos for each chapter in replacement of lecture, but he still has lectures to discuss articles. Lecture times are mostly for office hours. The biggest challenge was definitely understanding him because of his thick accent. He frequently made errors in his answer key for exams. The class's grading scale is nice though. 85+  A

The worst class I have ever taken in the econ department (which is saying a lot). Extremely boring, material is pointlessly difficult, class drones on and on. A 1.5 hour lecture feels like 5 years. Will NEVER take a class with this guy ever again
He always asks if anyone has questions and goes through the material slowly. Easy grader

analysis.name: Deirdre Bloome
