analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Horrible, worst experience I've had.  Took this to get out of a math credit since I'm not a math major, and it was ridiculously hard for an "elementary statistics" course.  Unclear in her lectures, lazy, and gives hard tests that look at whether or not you can read trick questions and teach yourself.
Kind of snotty. Would not recommend. The tests are rather easy, especially with the curve. Gives off that ivy-league grad vibe like she treats you like you're dumb.

I'm majoring in Sociology because I never wanted to take math again, so I was terrified of this course. Professor seemed intimidating at first, but also REALLY smart, helpful. By the end I really came to like stats and learned a lot about how to work w/ data. Make no mistake, this is hard material and you will be challenged. But the payoff is huge.

Professor Bloome is amazing! I was apprehensive to take this course because I don't like math, but I am so happy that I did. She explains topics to make sure that everyone understands. There isn't too much homework and if you put in the work it will pay off. She does research as well on gender income inequality which is great. Office hours are good

She was an amazing professor who made coding accessible while still teaching statistics basics in great lectures. The homework was purposeful and her grading was clear and helped you improve. She genuinely cared about all her students and our success and was ready to help people solve issues with content and the class in general. I learned a lot.

analysis.name: Benjamin Blankenship
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Ben's a great GSI! You can tell he cares about his students because he's always offering additional help, direct feedback, or walking around checking up on tables during lab. Best GSI I've had at UMich so far! Grades fairly (and according to rubric) and you can always ask for feedback on the papers. Prepared for class and office hours are flexible!

Ben was great for Psych393Polsci 330! He was so helpful, and always had examples in section to help students understand the lecture material. Also, he always had interactive activities in class to help students immerse themselves in the material. "Online" participation (via twitter) is fun. DEFINITELY TAKE THIS CLASS -if you like psych of politics

Ben was easily the best GSI that I have had at UMich. He came to class prepared, and he was always willing to answer students' questions or meet during office hours. He truly wanted his students to succeed, and his calm personality helped the class run smoothly even when discussing some of the more difficult topics. I would highly recommend him!
Solid GSI, makes a really boring David Winter lecture enjoyable. One of the better psychology GSIs that I have had at Michigan. Good grader

Ben is the best GSI I have ever hard. He is not so much as an "easy grader" but more so understanding and VERY FAIR considering the level of the course. He is very easy to talk to and responds promptly. He really looks out for student's best interest. I can't thank him enough for a great semester!!!!!!!! A+++++++++++++++++++++++++++

analysis.name: Eliot Bongionvanni
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: MATH 215 is an difficult class, due to Dr. Dunworth writing very hard HW and tests. However, Dr. B was an great professor given the circumstances. He taught very clearly and was great at answering questions. Unfortunately, he tended to rush through some lectures, and the problems he did in class were very easy and not reflective of the HW or exams.

Professor B was an incredible professor for Calc 3. This course is challenging, but I feel he explained it rather well. You can tell he has a passion for teaching and for Calc 3. His lectures are great, and he posts his notes. He is very accessible with office hours and via email. He also stays after class to answer questions. Highly recommend him!

Honestly I think prof. Bongiovanni is one of the best professors at Umich. He is so organized, prepared and passionate about what he is teaching in lectures. Furthermore he actually cares about his students and stays over a few extra minutes to answer any questions or doubts. WOULD DEFINITELY RECOMMEND ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS OUT THERE!!!!!

This class is super hard, but it's not really his fault. Dunworth writes the tests and homework and they are brutal. The curve was very good, but still a B average for the class. Dr. B is a nice guy and always ready to help, but sometimes he can rush during the lecture. Not a bad guy, just a horrible course in general.
Professor B was a very straightforward lecturer in 215 last semester. He was approachable and patient with my silly questions at office hours.

analysis.name: Mara Bollard
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Mara is a sweet teacher, easy to understand, and inspirational. She had daily participation quizzes and would give answers with thorough, helpful explanations in class. She's always willing to answer questions, especially during what she calls a "chat break" during each lecture. I would definitely take another class with her in the future!

Amazing professor. She is knowledgeable about her subject, and you can tell that she is passionate about it. She's very kind and approachable. The class has a small workload, with only a few exams, 5 homeworks, and a 3 question quiz every class, which you get the answers to in class. Exams make up most of your grade, so make sure you study.

Dr. Bollard's introductory cognitive science survey was a wonderful introduction to the discipline. We get a fairly broad but shallow overview of concepts in cognitive science, phil. of mind, ethics, decision theory, etc, and they are unified in an interesting and memorable way. This course is a good way to gauge your interest in cognitive science.

Bollard was a great professor! She made lectures pretty easy to understand, and she was very passionate on cog sci! Your grade is based on lecture quizzes (which we discuss in class so it's pretty much easy perfect scores), 2 exams and a final, and 5 homeworks (best out of 4). Honestly, just study well & you'll be good. Take this class w her !!

Honestly stopped caring about this class after I P/F but Mara seems super sweet and you can tell she knows her stuff. Sometimes things can be a bit unclear, but for the most part she's decent! Lectures were a bit boring sometimes but honestly the accent makes it more engaging lol the guest lecturer she brought in for a bit def was not the best tho

analysis.name: Bogdan Popa
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Honestly one of the best professors I've had in the ME department. He really cares about you actually learning the material instead of memorizing or trying to use pattern recognition to solve problems. Exams are very resonable. He's also pretty good at explaining stuff.

Another perspective which is completely opposite of the review below me. The class was great. The exams are easy, he grades lightly, and he wants to help you learn the material. He is an overall nice professor who definitely cares about learning his students' names. I loved that Professor Popa went into depth in the derivation of formulas.

Prof. Popa is a very calm and collected person who explains material very clearly and at an appreciable pace. His exams can get tricky at times, but he grades based mostly on process, so arithmetic errors aren't a huge concern on exams. He also has two engaging MATLAB group projects which further our understanding of the course material.

Overall a nice guy who knows his stuff and teaches well. Made a point to learn the students' names. Very responsive to feedback. For example, some students asked that we work on more examples and he dedicated Fridays to working on exam style questions. Easy to reach at office hours. Exams, grading, and grading scale all very fair.

He is a very understandable professor. Content is tricky, but he teaches everything in a way where if you follow his steps, you will get a lot of partial credit on the exam even if you mess up. Care about students performing well, and will bump grades if you are close to cut-offs.

analysis.name: James Bodiford
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bodiford was fantastic. He explained all the material clearly and thoroughly and was clearly very passionate about the subject. As long as you attend classes, you should get an A with very little difficulty. It's an interesting class if you're interested in music and science fiction, my favorite class I've taken at UMich!

At first I thought James was super dull in his teachings, but as the class material gets more interesting so does he. There were a ton of hilarious moments in the class and I'd definitely take James again if I was doing another music class.

Great class, great professor, the sci fi section is phenomenal! I will say though, highly reccomend you attend lectures so you won't fall behind in contents, which honestly I didn't have an issue with because the lectures are so easy to digest.

Fantastic professor and a fantastic course. The lectures were quite interesting and I learned a ton. Assignments are easy too and the projects were actually quite fun to work on as well. My only gripe is he sometimes cuts off people answering questions, and then later gets upset when no one raising their hand to answer questions. But yea he's cool.
Good professor and interesting lectures if you enjoy the content, but he grades a little stricter than I thought

analysis.name: Steven Bogaerts
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE FOR EECS 492! The class has been completely revamped and there is double the content crammed into the course with more depth and harder exams. The exams are nothing like whats shown in lecture. And this man just glosses over every mathematical formula during lecture like its nothing. Don't take this class or you will regret it.

DO NOT TAKE EECS492. This is the most content dense class I've ever taken. As an INTRO class, there is enough content to divide this course into two different ones. Exams are unfair and nothing like the practice ones. Lectures were packed with content and equations/graphs that were not talked about enough. Take 442, 388, or 445 instead.

While EECS 492 definitely got harder than past semesters, Professor Bogaerts was a great lecturer. He was very caring and thoroughly answered questions in class. I highly recommend going to class in person, as the content is a lot more digestible this way!

Despite provided online lecture, I went to in-person lecture just for Bogaerts. He was always kind and inspirational and you could tell he really wanted us to succeed. Although attendance was low in lecture, he always taught with the same amount of vigor and passion. His mantra "you belong here" actually helped me a lot over the semester.

Lectures were very informational and engaging. He obviously cares about the material and his students, and is very accessible outside of class hours. Great teacher for EECS 280, as long as you pay attention to lectures then you should be prepared for everything. He makes every student feel valued, and is willing to answer any question.

analysis.name: Bobby Madamanchi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Excellent lecturer for the data-oriented mastery course. Allows for a good deal of flexibility within the project specifications and provides ample support during and outside of class. Allows students to really concentrate on the project all semester and minimizes distractions. Provides time in class for group work, if needed. Good guest speakers.

Great professor and overall good guy, can be a bit experimental and freeform with lecture style and content, but the material is overall solid stuff - definitely helpful for high level coding patterns.

Beyond that, he has very clear grading criteria and is happy to help you do the best you can. 10/10 would take again.
The format of this class really didn't work for me - it was hard to follow along with what was happening. More structure would have been better.

Attend half of the lectures and get all late penalties waived, an absolutely wild deal but helps immensely with planning around other classes! This also means grading will take longer. Many assignments have clear rubrics and extra credit opportunities. He'll help prep for coding interviews, and the labs try too. Lab time could be made more valuable

analysis.name: Bryan Roby
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Roby is a professor I had the displeasure of ending up with. His grading criteria are incredibly unclear and his approach to teaching is "life doesn't give you a syllabus." His lectures are dependant on information he expects you to learn on your own (that he doesn't tell you about) and there is barely a common theme in the class.

Bryan Roby is an absolute legend. Literally the smartest professor in his field. You will be suprised how much you learn about Judaism in North Africa. I went into the class with no ambition and proceeded to write one of the greatest essays of my life. Please take him if you can, he's so amazing and this was my favorite class ever at Michigan.

Professor Roby is the best non-engineering professor I have had at the University of Michigan. Workload is light, the class is super revolved around participation and engagement which I love. He really cares for the students and he makes you realize that the main goal for this class isn't to get an A but actually learn the Judaic content.
Professor Roby is very understanding and really is just looking for people to engage in class discussion. If you just participate in class you are almost guaranteed an A. Solid class.
One of the best professors I have ever had. Really caring and I really think he is one of many few professors who truly cares for their students and realizes we have lives outside of class.

analysis.name: Patrick Boland
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Pat is concise. He instills confidence into your mathematic abilities. Pat always encourages students to find real-world applicability within the material covered in class, which seems rare among professors here. Overall, Pat is fair, patient, and smart; my level of understanding within calculus has increased dramatically since I've taken his class

He connected all topics to real-life examples, which made class fun. He didn't really explain topics that well in class - you are expected to do the readings/videos in order to learn in-depth. But, he was always accessible during office hours and genuinely made an effort to connect with you!

Pat does an amazing job of creating a light-hearted and constructive learning environment! This was my first calculus class at Michigan, and I am confident that this gave me a good foundation going forward. Highly recommend taking his section of Math 115 if you can!

Professor Boland is easily the best professor I've had at UMich. He's an engaging lecturer, helpful outside of class, and is overall a really great guy. He helped me through a very hard time in my college career and while my performance in this course wasn't what I had hoped, he was very reassuring and available to help me out.

Highly recommend taking Boland for 216. He is a great lecture and makes class interesting. Lecture and recitation do not have mandatory attendance, but both are basically necessary for doing well in the course. Boland knows what he is talking about and is very accessible with office hours as well.

analysis.name: David Brang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Definitely recommend for those who need a psych/neuro lab req. Lecture is not mandatory, exams are all open note, with free internet access and can be taken anywhere. Problem sets were intimidating at first because of the online software, but students are given step-by-step instructions on how to get full points.

Gave very dense, thorough lectures. It is clear he knows a lot about the field. Lecture content definitely went over my head at some points, but overall a good lecturer and clearly cares about his students.

He's a nice guy, clear slides and easy exams. The only issue is that he is extremely boring. His voice is super monotone and SOOOO slow, I would watch his lectures on 2x speed and be fine. I literally only went to the very first lecture and got an A in the class. It's an easy A but only take it if you're actually interested in EEG/want to study it

The course material is dense but he explains it in a way that makes it way easier. The exams weren't too hard and you can make a cheat sheet for them. He puts indicators on slides to tell which are the most important and which are background info, which makes studying for the exams very easy. Overall an excellent professor and course :)

Pretty nice guy. Only had 1 lecture a week, so not too much to gauge. The majority of the time he is just lecturing at you to get all the content in for you to use in the lab portion. The slides are crowded, but he usually provides the pdf with builds.
The lab isn't bad but that might depend on your GSI, and there's one partner presentation.

analysis.name: Mark Brehob
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 97 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: In my own view, this lecturer simple does not know the material at all. He is not clear in his presentation of the material and is very unhelpful and negative with respect to students' academic objectives.
He speaks extremely fast. He frequently jumps between different points but always fails to mention the connections. He is helpful during office hours and caring though.

Surprised by some of the negative reviews here, especially regarding insensitivity. I'm black and I've never felt any sort of racism from Brehob. He's an incredible lecturer. He's hilarious, and he knows his stuff. He's got great OH, and he really cares about his students. A top-tier professor.

Amazing kind and respectful teacher. The best teacher I have interacted with at umich in general, he is so sweet kind and respectful. I have never met a teacher like him and honestly I am so happy I took it with him during this semester and not beaumont even though I know he's also good. Extremley underrated and amazing professor! Take him!!
I cannot understand what his accent. Maybe it's too difficult for an international student. His tone makes me wanna sleep too.

analysis.name: Pamela Brandwein
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: By far the best professor I have had. I learned so much in this class and I genuinely had so much fun during lecture. I was looking forward to class every week. A lot of reading and the grading is tough, but definitely worth it.

Dr. Brandwein is the best professor I have had by a landslide. Her lectures are very engaging and she is extremely knowledgeable. On top of that, she takes the time to learn her students names and gets to know them, which I have found rare at such a big school. Grading is harsh, but that is dependent on your GSI as she doesn't grade directly.

Professor Brandwein is amazing! One of the best classes I have taken at U of M! So interesting, she is seriously a wealth of knowledge. Go to office hours! Hard class but if you work hard you can do well! Totally worth the work!

Prof. Brandwein is absolutely wonderful. Lectures are extremely engaging. Class time passed very quickly. Material is very interesting especially if there is interest in the subject. She doesn't use powerpoints in class though, so I would recommend actually going to class (though she doesn't take attendance). One of my favorite profs & class at UM.

Pamela is one of the best professors I have ever had at the University of Michigan. Though her class challenged me, it was extremely eye opening and profound. She pushes her students to learn through analysis and discovery rather than just giving you the answer, and left me wanting to make the world a better place. Her passion is contagious.

analysis.name: Brian Porter
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 95 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Amazing lectures,he plays into your assumptions about history then completely breaks them. he is stricter about having no technology in class/respectful class environment and is not afraid to call you out, but I don't think thats a negative. the grading requirements are simple, just do the reading, quizzes, and weekly assignment and you are golden.

I took this class for a SS distribution requirement, and I'm happy with choosing it.  Professor Porter was clearly passionate about the material, yet I will confess that many lectures drag if you don't have a particular interest in this topic.  However, you don't have to go to all of them, and you can still get an easy A with minimal work overall.

This was a pretty difficult class, and definitely not worth it if you're just looking for a SS distribution in your first year. That said, it's one of the most interesting classes I've taken in a while, and taught me so much about the economy that really should have been covered in ECON 101. Love this prof, and I definitely recommend the class.

No exams, point-based. There are 56 total points and each assignment is one point and you need 53 points to have an A. 40ish pages of reading, discussion, quiz, and essay (500 words), I enjoyed everything because he makes lectures really interesting and I found the topic interesting, put in the work and you'll be fine, but not a blow-off class

Professor Porter will probably remain my favorite professor in my umich experience - he is super passionate about the subject and his lectures make a lot of sense but I'd recommend taking a lot of notes. If you don't attend lecture you won't pass the quizzes or the class. He forever changed my perspective on history so I can't recommend him enough!

analysis.name: Michael Burke
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I made a rate my professor account just to write nice things about this guy. If you have an opportunity to take 290 with him TAKE IT!!! He always made himself available for questions, told fun stories about his experience in the industry and he takes time to get to know all of his students.

Professor Burke is a fantastic instructor and provides excellent in-class teaching that correlates to real-world experiences in production. I would highly recommend taking this course with Burke if you are looking for impactful criticism, support, and guidance related to all things writing, editing, and production!

This was my favorite professor of my first year of college, he is so caring and understanding. I went through a very rough time mentally during his class and missed alot of lectures and he still made sure i understood everything we were doing. Love this guy so much

Michael Burke was one of the best professors I have had at UMich. He is the coolest guy and taught us so much about the industry through his own experience and by producing ourselves. There are 2 group projects outside of class, but they generally take only a day each and are super fun. Take his class!!!!!

Best professor I have had at school thus far. Always helpful and available whenever you need it. Understanding when things go wrong. Offers great feedback and teaches the content incredibly. I'd give more than 5 stars if I could.

analysis.name: Heidi Buchele
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Heidi was tough, but when you're getting a license to help save lives, you have to be. She was excellent at providing feedback and facilitating class participation. I would take her class over and over again!

Heidi was a really fun professor to teach emergency response. This class has a lot of hands on activities and you have to go to class in order to get the certifications at the end of the semester. Each person (with a partner) gives a presentation for two topics in the course but as long as you meet with her she will tell you what to include.

Professor Heidi is very educated. She teaches everything very well and you will leave this class very educated. I loved this class for learning more about how to care for emergencies. She does make sure to practice a lot with us; but she does expect us to know the answers and she is pretty caring for situations. She will let you make up if needed
This class was fun, and Heidi is a good teacher. However, she can be loud and sometimes it may feel as though her comments on your work is personal (it's not, that is just her teaching style).

While it is easy to get an A and more of a fun class, Heidi is stressful to have as a teacher. She consistently calls on random people to answer questions but also gets mad at pretty much anything anyone does. I guess it can be good for learning but I found her to be pretty rude and impatient most of the time. Her class definitely is an experience.

analysis.name: Dominique Butler-Borruat
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took French235 but wasn't an option to choose. He was a really nice teacher and very caring. He is willing to meet with students outside of class and is very helpful. He takes note of who participates and often cold calls so I'd recommend answering questions when you feel confident so he doesn't call on you, then it's pretty chill. Overall great

Dominique is a great professor. She's really sweet and kind, and she's aware of how boring grammar lessons can be so she does try to throw in some jokes or break up the monotony, which is appreciated. She always has office hours and is very accessible by email.

Dominique is an okay professor whose classes are made great by her personality. She is such a caring teacher who genuinely wants every student to succeed. Her teaching methods do not work well for me. I felt like the RC teaches you half of a French class. Lectures covered the material in a way that made no sense to me. She's still an angel though.
Dominique is a very fun and caring professor. She's very easy to meet with outside of class, and she does her best to make grammar presentations fun.

Dominique is one of the best professors I've had so far! She makes it clear that she wants everyone to succeed and will devote as much time as necessary to make sure every student is at their desired level. Her feedback is extremely thorough and she always lets students know what they need to work on the most.

analysis.name: John Buckley
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Outside of some lectures feeling useless, every lecture is engaging. John Buckley is hilarious and he doesn't even realize it. Everything in his life is so bizarre but in a cool way. He wants everyone to be a great writer and he is very passionate about what he teachers. You will learn the best from him if you listen to him and follow what he says

Professor Buckley was super chill, and his course really challenged my perspectives on homelessness. Very reading-heavy in the beginning and writing-heavy at the end, so complete optional assignments early on. He is a fair grader who makes it easy to get an A if you try; I would definitely recommend his class!

Professor Buckley was a great teacher who truly taught me to think a lot more about the unhoused populations and the many circumstances that lead to homelessness. Through this class, I was able to learn more about Groundcover News. The only critique of this class is that it's a lot of peer reviewing. Optional assignments are necessary.
Sometimes professor Buckley's assignments are unclear, but he is extremely caring and willing to work with people. The class itself is not hard if you participate, and Buckley is a great guy.
John is a great professor; focuses more on effort and actually spending time being thoughtful with the material versus grading. Offers extra credit.

analysis.name: Nathan Byrne
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This writing class was disappointing. The instructor rarely gave feedback or graded assignments on time, and when feedback was requested, he dismissed it as unnecessary. His teaching style was unprofessional, often unprepared, and at times awkwardly personal. I expected much higher standards from my university.

I've never had a professor that seemed to have no idea what he was talking about the whole time yet still decided to host hour and a half long lectures in an ART class. He confused himself so often and his directions for projects made no sense. He also never knew how to use the softwares he made us use. Learned nothing from him.
While Nathan is super lenient with his grading criteria, he makes you do A LOT for most of these projects. It was super difficult for me to be able to find time to do any of these assignments.

analysis.name: Eunshin Byon
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She prepared very carefully and orderly. I did not know why so many bad comments on her!! She is originally Korean, I guess. But not easy to get A, we need to write FAST in exam!!

Professor Byon was an okay teacher, slight accent did make her tough to understand. The exams were strangely difficult, and hard to do within the time limit. Didn't finish either midterm or final in time and my grade took a hit. Class was annoying but it was more because I had a heavy course load. Don't underestimate the exams!

Very nice lady; has an Asian accent so takes a second to follow but not incomprehensible.  Grades fairly easily, material is relatively straightforward, and exams are open-book, open-note.  Also gave us a couple of bonus point opportunities, including class attendance.

She had really detailed lecture slides. Her lectures helped explain everything real well. The best part is that exams were OPEN NOTE AND OPEN BOOK. It doesn't matter how the professor is at that point, its a great class.

Not particularly difficult. My issue is directed more at the IOE department for placing more than 3 midterms for core classes over the same week. I got a lower score on the midterm, and it's going to hurt me a lot since exams are worth 80% of your grade. Other downside is you don't really learn anything practical or hands-on (no projects).

analysis.name: Michael Byers
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Class was easy, but professor is arrogant and not very helpful.

Horrible course - the grading is completely subjective and prompts are not clear. Do not take fiction into film, ESPECIALLY if you aren't an english major. Also, no communication between the professors, or between the professors and GSIs, which means you have no idea who your audience is going to be and can't get any reasonable help for the papers.

Byers is funny, intelligent, quirky, and interesting.  He attempts to learn everyones name even though it's a decent sized lecture.  He's adorable in a geeky way, very helpful and has a stellar reading list.  He alludes to Star Wars almost every day.   An A is easily attainable if you do the readings.  Highly recommended course!

WONDERFUL! I've had so many bad creative writing professors I've really considered dropping it. Prof. Byers is completely different. The class isn't just endless workshops & reading short stories for no reason. He really teaches how to write (by showing how others write) and is encouraging and helpful. Every Creative Writing subcon should have him.

Michael was phenomenal. Had a great if incredibly intense reading list, reading quizzes on each book to check that everyone read. Led discussions really well but didn't always focus on the literary aspects, also focused on the larger picture or even sometimes the literary tools. Only 2 papers were fiction based on truth -- fun and different. 10/10

analysis.name: James Casey Jr.
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Casey was a great course coordinator. Most of the work is done in class (except for small weekly quizzes), and the four larger projects were pretty interesting and not overbearing. Labs were a mix of data analysis and animal experiments, and most didn't take the full four hours. Bio226 is definitely my favorite lab class I've taken here so far!

Dr. Casey was nice, accessible, and explained concepts clearly. However, he tended to misspeak sometimes which made things confusing. His memorization questions on exams were simple, but his application questions were incredibly difficult. They felt beyond the scope of this course, but he was fair in removing them/giving partial credit.

He is definitely better than Haenfler when it comes to explaining material. I like the way he lectures. The final exam was very difficult. 80 questions with intense application-based questions that required a lot of thinking outside of what we learned in class. 4th exam had a lot of spelling errors and didn't look like it was revised.

This class is really hard for some reason. Exams often ask unfair questions that contradict what we learned in class. He is pretty good with dropping questions/giving partial credit. However, the time I spend studying for the class is not representative in the grading at all.

Good lecturer. The class is content heavy so the exams are difficult. You get extra credit from submitting questions on piazza. Has ocassional choose all that apply questions that are difficult. Starts class right at the start time with an iclicker question. iclicker is graded. Class has case studies done in groups before every exam.

analysis.name: Brian Malley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 376 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Tried to talk to Professor Malley about my circumstances and confusion in the class, and straight up insulted me. I attended lectures and discussions frequently and learned nothing of substance from this class. No intro psych class should be structured the way Professor Malley has this class set up. Get these professors off of their high horses.

Though quizzes are open note, you are expected to remember every small detail from lecture. The questions can be ambiguous and he refuses to acknowledge that. I don't understand why we are paying over 100 bucks for the textbook when it is rarely even used and he admits that a good portion is irrelevant. Overall, difficult professor to work with.

While his lectures are interesting, the quizzes can be extremely confusing. He requires very specific terminology in a single sentence. Be prepared to rewatch lectures and take DETAILED notes. If you get a bad grade the first time, don't be too stressed; People tend to do better as time goes on. As a whole, really hard for an introductory course.

Had weird and inappropriate comments with most of the content, always making things sexual to be funny?? Also, the quizzes were immediate fails if you didn't have the key terms he was looking for. Only good thing about this class is that there is no final exam.

You have several open note quizzes throughout the class, drop the lowest score, they are open note. His grading criteria is a bit strange, but he does offer some extra credit here and there. Have a good relationship with your GSI because a lot of answers come from discussion. Textbook is online. The lectures are boring, but it is important to go

analysis.name: Carly Nowicki
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 89 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: i ain't even out of her class yet and im already so sick of these papers. labs aren't hard at all, its the follow-up assignments that'll kill you. plus its wild that your grade is determined basically by your exams, since lab attendance doesn't count for much. shes also incredibly passive aggressive and her lectures feel like shes yelling at you.

While Dr. Nowicki could be condescending at times, she always outlined exactly what was expected. The grading system was very forgiving, tests were fair, and there were lots of opportunities to get extra points. The field trips were super fun and engaging. Labs were a little tedious and were very dependent on your GSI (shoutout to my goat Kai).

If you've ever wanted to relive high school, this is the class. She talks to everyone like we're 15, polite yet condescending, and exams are so vague, it's just about decoding her wording. There are exams instead of lab practicals and way too many random assignments for a LAB course. Good luck, being a required class,sadly, there's no escaping her.

Her lectures really are not terrible, but I do not agree with the way that the class is structured at all. Nowicki requires us to stay in lab all 3 hours, regardless of productivity, and to be entirely honest--is not the friendliest. Honestly probably would take again if was the only choice, but def not on my own accord.

This class may seem easy, but the tests are confusing and full of trick questions. I read every recommended textbook section and still struggled. The content isn't hard, but the way it's assessed is unfair. Nowicki often didn't know answers to her own questions and made frequent mistakes in lectures and office hours.

analysis.name: Carleen Hsu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Hsu is extremely unclear about grades. There are no graded assignments. Your grade is based peer reviews from sets. It's a LOT of outside work and time commitment, you must show up whenever and wherever. Professor Hsu gives no instructions. She assumes you know everything she wants. If you disagree with her, she will punish your grade.

If you don't know something or make a film differently than her specific perspective and preferences, your grade will be affected. Talks disrespectfully to students and her classes are not structured or clear. I would never take a class with her again.

Ling seemed like a nice person, but you definitely don't want to get on her bad side or else your grade will suffer. I ended up doing well in the class, but she's just not super clear on what she expects from you.

I love Ling (Carleen). I am 100% honest when I say that she is the best professor that I have EVER had here at the University of Michigan. As someone with an interest in production, she is transforming this department in the best way possible and giving us more opportunities. She will always be my first, best, and favorite mentor.

One of my favorite professors! She is incredibly smart and skilled, and has impressive knowledge and experience in film so she gives really meaningful feedback. She is personable and loves motivating students to grow and be their best. I appreciated how she made sure her class was a supportive environment for making mistakes and learning from them.

analysis.name: Carina Ray
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: All other reviews are very accurate. Disheartening, passive aggressive, and confusing to say the least. Very picky but also disorganized and often blames said disorganization on students. Doesn't really know how to work canvas and often blames this on students as well. Essentially she's doing too much for what the class is. Take any other class.
Very passive aggressive. Not good at communicating. Provides feedback that varies based on assignment, so it's hard to get a good grade. Doesn't know the material in class.

For a three credit, 100-level history course, this class is very demanding, with unclear grading policies. She doesn't know how to use canvas, and complains about students not reading the syllabus, yet the syllabus is not updated and often changes as she pleases. Although she is very knowledgeable in her area, she can be very passive aggressive.

Ray knows about Africa but doesn't transmit that throughout the class given that students choose the modules (often things she's unfamiliar with and students barely care about). Very passive aggressive and complains about students' boredom but doesn't nothing to help it. Lots of work and unclear grading standards. Inconsistent class overall.
Unhelpful, provides criticism but nothing constructive.

analysis.name: Cameron Gibelyou
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: An extremely caring professor! Lectures were never dull and always left me in reflection when the class period ended. I gained so much more than an understanding of Popular Science from his course. Truly made to be a professor, his public speaking, storytelling, and personal experience were phenomenal and furthered our comprehension of the topic.

So nice and we always had great in-class discussions. His class made me more reflective and think deeper about myself and the world around me. Incredibly easy grader and really cares about his students. One of my favorite classes I have taken at UofM

Cameron was a kind and respectful professor. His class was very easy and interesting. However, I thought the topic would be more focused on popular science but it was actually heavily focused on religion. He doesn't hide the fact that he's religious, which isn't bad, but I was uncomfortable with how much it influenced the course content.

Class with Cameron is great. I took Predicting the Future with him and can say it has been one of my favorite after 3 years as a student. Beside the interesting subject, Cameron strives to make the class relevant and encourages class feedback throughout the course. If you have the time, take this class! Definitely manageable/easy workload too.
Awesome guy and a good class to learn about how to work in the real world.

analysis.name: Caroline New
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is very funny and she made class exciting. I did not know anything about translation but when the readings were hard she made it easy to understand. The work is not really hard it is just that it is hard to get an A+.

If you have the chance, take a class with Professor New. She cares a lot about her students and wants to see them succeed and develop their writing skills. She always made the classes exciting and allowed us to really take creative control over our assignments. I think she is teaching creative writing now!

Professor New always makes you feel heard, and I felt like I could say anything without being judged. She is very kind and you can tell she cares a lot about her students. Even though some of the assignments were hard, she broke them down every time we had questions until we understood.
She's super sweet and a really good poet and teacher; her classes are easy and fun!

analysis.name: Celia Schultz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was a massive disappointment (and I love the topic). So many tedious writing assignments and extremely pointless 20-minute timed essays. Discussion is useless. Very picky grading. Lectures are impossible to follow with essentially no slides and a copious amount of rambling. If you want to learn about Rome, take CLCIV 202 or HISTORY 201.

I had her for CLCIV 302- Worst class of my academic career. She was the most boring lecturer of all time. Furthermore, she made us buy her expensive book to read from. The check-ins were worth 40% of the class and they were graded like they were the most important thing since Jesus. absolutely terrible. Readings were never ending. Never take her.

She's a nice person, but the class was pretty rough. We had four 20-minute in-class essays. Her slides are AWFUL so if you don't show up, you won't understand anything. The slides have barely any words and she talks a ton. The final is key terms (there are hundreds given to us- impossible), a timeline, two essays, and a huge map all in two hours.

Highlights: -5% of class grade reduced if you miss "spot-check" attendance -Grading based on ability to regurgitate exactly what she says in lecture (word for word) -Expects you to memorize an insane amount of information -Doesn't post slides I'm a student taking 18 academic credits and this 4 credit course was over half of the reading I had to do

Professor Schultz does a great job balancing the totality of Roman Monarchical and Republican History with fun and engaging lectures.  The course is extremely content-dense, but she manages to break it up into nice chunks that are supported by primary source readings. She also does a good job of making the course AI proof, so lectures are 100% req.

analysis.name: Amy Cell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: A great lecturer! Definitely new to teaching but super knowledgable and ready to help her students.

She gives everyone A, only her 'favorites' will get A+. She intentionally changed my marks from 10/10 to 0/10 after 1 month just so I could get an A as I wasn't her favorite student. I emailed her and she said she did it by mistake and that she will revert it but never did that. Everyone else gets A too, had I known that I wouldn't have put efforts

Her lectures are amazing. She has so much experience being out in the corporate world, managing people and projects. Almost every lecture had an anecdote from her past work with a strong message. The group project and class blend really well. You actually apply what you learn from her lecture while working with your client.

Overall a great class if you are an engineering grad student who needs a course to reach full time status, balance your course load, and boost your GPA. Attendance is graded, so don't plan on skipping class regularly. However, the lectures are interesting and worth attending. Easy A if you do the work.

analysis.name: Carlos Cesnik
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Cesnik was a great professor.  He really cared about the students, and that showed through.  Unfortunately I took it at 8:30 AM, so the students weren't terribly energetic which frustrated him, but he's super helpful and really wants you to learn.  Sure, it's challenging material, but work with him, and you can master it.

If you're like myself and most people and can't stand structures, take this guy. He's probably the best possible structures prof. you can get, though it's not a very easy class by any means. Don't get the book, you won't need it. At least I didn't. He has pretty good notes, so unfortunately you can't miss his class.

Prof. Cesnik is one of the better profs I've had so far at Michigan.  He is a very likable guy and he knows the subject very well.  The class is not that difficult if you go to lecture and take good notes...the book is worthless so don't waste your money.

He's quite famous for structure guy but NEVER for 481. I'm doubtful if he fully understands what he is teaching, as he often leaves the lecture to GSIs from Prof. Martins' lab. Seriously with Prof. Martins were teaching this semester as usual.
Good guy but pretty heinous class. He asks questions on exams that are way harder than we can be expected to complete in the given time. I was lucky to escape with an A-

analysis.name: Abigail Celis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: In her first semester at Penn State, she surprised me with her course. I'm a senior in a 100 level French history elective, and her class was doable. If you come to class prepared, and engage in the class, its an easy A. No textbook required. Shes a soft spoken prof, and willing to help her students, you just have to be willing to put in work.

Celis is a professor who is a little more soft spoken, but is knowledgeable about her subject.  Shes got a good sense of humor if you participate and engage in class.  Her grading is fair, but the work load is heavy, and she cares that you come prepared with the homework.  Overall, she made a subject I'm not crazy about pretty bearable.

Overall her class just bored me to tears. I was really interested to take a class about hipsters because its such an unconventional topic, but everything she talked about was so generic it made me not even want to do the work (which was way too heavy for a freshman seminar anyway).
She's soft-spoken and she is a really nice person.

analysis.name: Celeste Brusati
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's a really nice lady but she is a bit of a boring lecturer. There is not much reading in the class, but the finals require a ton of memorization. Interesting subject matter though.

Celeste rarely actually lectures in her own class, which seems pretty backwards. Frequent quest speakers and sometimes the quest speakers give no relevant information in their lectures. Nice person, but not an overwhelmingly good teacher. She's also obsessed with Dutch painters, so get ready to hear a lot about those.

She seemed like an ok professor but she never really lectured. There was almost always a guest lecturer so we never knew what we were going to get during class. Some were interesting, some were boring. The exams aren't hard, as long as you study describing paintings with friends. The exam questions were all brand new, so there was nothing to review

She has certain things expected from each student. When I went to her office hour to consult with my research paper, she gave many (not that helpful) resources. You have to figure out what she wants to see in your paper. This class was a small-size seminar type class held once a week so if you skip one, she will definitely notice.
One of those Shaman Drum-only hippies.  Not terribly organized, but overall not bad.

analysis.name: Erin Cech
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cech has opened my mind to so much in the course of Sociology/Women's Studies 447. She is very extremely intelligent, respectful, and professional. Her lectures are always organized and intriguing. I've been recommending this course to everyone. Honestly, this has been my favorite course so far, and I'm not a Soc or Women's Studies major.

Professor Cech is AMAZING. Soc 447 has been the best class I have taken so far. She provided really interesting material in lecture that was different than I have gotten in most soc/women's studies classes. She is really nice and energetic. Reading material and attending class is a must because she doesn't post slides online. But totally worth it!

Easily the best class I've taken here.  She's super nice and professional and intelligent and all of the course material was engaging.  She's also receptive to student feedback and actually seems to enjoy teaching unlike some of the profs at this university.
Sociology of Gender was my favorite class of the semester due to the interesting lectures and readings as well as Professor Cech's sunny disposition. Take a class with her if you can.

analysis.name: Rosario Ceballo
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS, ESPECIALLY IF YOU ACTUALLY LIKE CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY. She might as well be teaching counseling psych, calls people seeking mental health treatment "seriously disturbed" and puts questions on her exams about the color of M&M's in her story in class. Pointless, offensive, shouldn't be teaching clinical psychology.

I took this last semester and it was AWFUL.  She had no compassion for mentally ill patients and made that very clear.  Also, she is incredibly detail oriented in all the worst ways.  She basicallye xpects you to memorize details so long as they have no thing to do with anything else.  HORRIBLY BORING, also.

This class was very detail specific.  Only really 3 grades count (2 exams and a movie paper) not much to help if you do bad on the first exam.  It's a small lecture class, although there is no attendence if you miss class, you miss a lot.  The book is important and takes a lot straight from the book.

One of the hardest Psych class I've taken simply because Dr. Ceballo writes very detailed exams.  Although we don't have a textbook, she assigns a LOT of supplemental readings and expects you to memorize the details.  The exams questions are very specific regarding the assigned readings.

Really interesting course. She is really nice and makes lectures interesting. Essays are fun to write but she does grade harshly. Exams are very detail specific and tough. Definitely do the readings and go to class and take notes!!! But overall I do recommend the class(:

analysis.name: Ronald Caldwell
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 266 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I love Ron to death. He's a great guy and explains everything super well. His slides are great and he prepares you well for his exams. There isn't a ton of homework and he posts optional practice sets to help you understand the material. He's engaging and easy to follow. He cares about his students and wants everyone to understand the material!

Caldwell was a great choice for Econ 101. He's funny and made lectures enjoyable to go to. Would definitely take again. The one thing I would say is to take the exams SUPER seriously right out the gate. I bombed the first one and kind of blew my chances of getting an A right off the bat. Pay attention to that and you'll do fine.

Ron is a great prof who not only knows his material but knows how to help students understand the concepts. I don't think lectures were mandatory but you should really go. He occasionally hints at things on the exam and they are helpful in general. The hard part of this class is every question wrong on the exams is a percent off your overall grade.

Caldwell is the man. If you took econ in high school and did well on the AP tests, trust me, take Ron. Three tests throughout the year with just 30 mc questions. Even if you didn't take econ, his lectures are very good and he explains the information well. However, you may need to go in for help a few times... econ isn't a walk in the park.

Caldwell is the man. He makes Economics interesting and likes to joke with his classes. He's the first professor I've seen at Michigan that knows the names and has a personal relationship with students in a big lecture. It's a difficult, but if you go to lecture and discussion and do the problem sets, it will pay off and it will be worth it

analysis.name: Henry Chai
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very chill guy, makes jokes at lecture. Gives a bunch of practice problems during lecture to help students practice.
Very engaging lectures; professor genuinely cares about his students. Class is very manageable if practice problems are done without cheating.
Guy is engaging and knows what he is talking about and also super chill

analysis.name: Edward Chang
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 181 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Chang was awesome! He made this big 250+ class an open discussion course. Five exams, no papers or projects, and easy extra credit offered! 11 five question pop quizzes and tells you what section to study! Must read the textbook to do well on exams, but they're fair. Doesn't use CTools (no notes posted) and no electronics in class. Great class!

He believes that he is a liberal arts teacher, but does not teach in a progressive and meaningful way. He hosts lectures that give information pertaining to his childhood and life experiences, but dont help in the understanding or learning of content. His tests are extremely difficult and have nothing to do with what he teaches. He wasted my time.

Professor Chang is a great lecturer.  He acts tough, but he's a nice guy.  Gave out a fair amount of extra credit.  Must attend class and read the book to get an A.  Gives a half a point for speaking in class, and does want to hear from his students.  Take advantage of it. I missed an A- by a single point because I didn't speak two more times.

Dr. Chang is a good lecturer who told interesting stories about his work experience. There is a big emphasis on the textbook. I sometimes felt like we were not tested on the main concepts, but rather, on random details from both the textbook and lecture. Going to class and reading the textbook are both very important for success in the class.

I have never met someone who talks about themself as much as Chang.  What an ego.  The exams are extremely difficult in this class, and he does not allow tech in class.  No canvas notes.  I had to miss class because of a family function, and he would not give me the notes because it wasn't a life-or-death emergency.

analysis.name: Hakki Erdem Cipa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Erdem really cares about his students and will force them to put in effort.  Some may see this as him being harsh, but he is such a funny and happy guy it is clear he does it from a place of passion. He can grade not harshly but accurately, and will deduct your grade for missing more than 1 class, but overall you learn a ton and want more

I absolutely hated this class. While I expect history courses to be reading heavy he did not tie the material together at all. This would be fine if he was approachable in office hours or outside of class, and while he always says his door is open he is not open to conversation at all. Grades are arbitrarily given and he doesn't give good feedback.

He is extremely passionate about his subject. He made a dry topic like Turkish politics very interesting, especially for someone like who has had no background in Turkish history and politics. The readings assigned for this class were very challenging but interesting at the same time.

he's the goat and i can't recommend him enough, he gives out candy every lecture and is super smart, he cares about his students a lot. participation and effort matter but just showing up and doing the reading is enough. LOVES his wife also

He is traditional, doesn't like phones and doesn't give homework because of AI. So grade is just participation (which is very important) and 2 exams. He is a great professor and will help you if you need. Also gives candy in class

analysis.name: Cindy Schipani
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Schipani was an incredible corporate governance professor.  She was one of the most knowledgable professors on actual subject mater I have ever had.  Would absolutely recommend any course with her.

BL510 has been the easiest class of my graduate school career. I have already used the skills learned in this class before graduating, it is useful for many aspects of life outside of BL. You CANNOT miss a single class or make up the in-class assignments. Make sure you can be at every class session or else drop the class.
Ross should consider hiring a more 'in touch' professor. Content was remedial and could be taught by anyone with a J.D.
A true Gem of a course and professor!!!!!!

Professor Schipani presents herself in a very unprofessional manner. She is rude to her students, unhelpful, and fails to understand the hectic lifestyle of a college student. Highly recommend not taking a course with her.

analysis.name: Louis Cicciarelli
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Made class fun and interesting, lenient with deadlines, super caring, and always there to help when you need it. Cares a lot about his students and always open to talk. Best professor and def a good first year writing requirement to take if u have a heavy class load already.

Louis is great, he honestly made my semester so much better and is such a good professor when it comes to actually helping out students who need it. He didn't pressure us, due dates were flexible, as long as you put in effort and showed that you cared about/tried at the work he gives, you'll be great.
really great overall teacher! super upbeat - not too much homework and genuinely cares about students :)!

Super all around great guy. Really strives to hear your voice in your writing and encourages creative thinking in your work. You can tell he is genuinely passionate about his work and wants to see you succeed. I definitely recommend Louis for any student looking for a FYW professor.

FABULOUS professor! Absolutely LOVED this course. Louis is extremely funny and very dedicated to his students. The last two assignments of the course were creative essays- something I haven't done since middle school and they were extremely fun to write. Not a lot of homework, readings were simple. No tests and only four essays. HIGHLY recommend!

analysis.name: Cindy Lustig
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Did not give grading rubric for discussion posts. Grades seemed to be randomly assigned for these. Test review sheets did not match what was being tested. Expected full participation from a class of 60 students. If you did not participate, you got no credit. Extra credit was for test prep team assignments that pitted students against each other.

She tries...she really does...but something's just not working. I agree with all of the comments below. The lectures are horribly mind-numbing, and while she tends to spend a lot of time on less relevent things, she also glosss over rather important concepts. I'd recommend looking elsewhere.

wouldn't be so bad if she engaged the class during lecture more. the material itself has the potential to be interesting, but the way she presents it completely takes away any interest that i might have otherwise had. the fill-in-the-blank notes have no purpose other than making you come to lecture.  bad readings, unenthusiastic; a waste of time.

As mentioned, her lectures are painful (very) and she spends much too long on unecessary topics. Her approch to lecturing (reading right off her slides with little elaboration) is not condusive to learning and I would not recomend her to anyone. If you're going to take psych 240 please try to learn from another instructor.

the exams are reasonable, but the lecture is bad. She presents a lot of the more abstract concepts in a confusing way and shes not clear. the material is pretty interesting, but her lecures were not helpful to understand it.  she uses powerpoint and is not very interactive with the class.

analysis.name: John Ciorciari
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Other ratings are 20 years ago, hopefully newer ratings will not be removed. John's work is based on secondary research and case studies. He is shrewd, often unhelpful, needs external validation and decisions are not always based on work. Don't hold your breath if he promises your first publication as a graduate, protect your research.

Prof. Ciorciari is a fantastic professor! His lectures are clear, comprehensive and quite entertaining. He's also very approachable and loves talking to students about their careers. He makes the class relevant to your interests. Assignments are not difficult at all - just make sure you attend lecture and take solid notes. Highly reccommend!

John is a genius in about every way possible. He is knowledgeable about everything, and also is very nice, helpful, and approachable. Definitely go to his office hours- sometimes he throws out some great summer internship suggestions.

To be honest, GREAT PROF. Makes the lectures relevant, and is VERY willing to meet with students and discuss real stuff (e.g. careers/internships/goals). Very personable and fair. Assignments are explained very well.
He chooses assignments that are relevant to the career field. He is very approachable and interesting, often engages the class in discussion.

analysis.name: Sonya Dal Cin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Her exams are awful. She tests on specifics points in the readings (there are like 15 articles and 150 pgs of textbook readings for each exam) rather than overall main points. Worst part is she doesn't thing that anything is wrong. She thought a B- class average for the exam was "fine"... like what? That shouldn't happen for a 200 level class...

Terrible class but is easier than the other comm degree req classes... She's a terrible lecturer, literally reads off the slides. Going to lecture is not necessary because she posts the powerpoints online

This class was supposed to be about Mass Media and the Individual, but it really should be called "here memorize some random facts from a million journal articles". There is SO MUCH READING and exams are only on the journal articles. Fortunately there is a paper that takes a good chunk of your grade and the paper was easy, but the exams are awful

Professor Dal Cin finds happy mediums in all aspects of teaching: she is engaging and entertaining without being irritating, understanding without being too much of a pushover, and she made the class easy without being a blow-off. Dal Cin is much more concerned about whether or not you get the big picture than the obnoxious details. Great course.

After reading past ratings, I was kind of excited to take this class because I thought it'd be fairly easy. This was not the case - grades were complete wild cards and her exams were written to cover  little details of the theories and not the overall big picture or theories themselves. The paper was fine but the exams were really disheartening

analysis.name: Cindy Crawford
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Not a good professor. This class was somewhat useless, but it is in the core curriculum. Basically you have to be a favorite I guess. Even if you go to office hours to get help, she'll still give you median grade. The grading is so subjective it's not even funny. Also don't buy the textbook, we never used it.

I really liked Prof. Crawford! The curriculum and grading scale are controlled by Ross so those being really bad aren't her fault, but she really tries to engage her students and make sure that they learn something. Showing up to office hours is definitely super important in this class, and make sure you participate.
go to office hours. youll get an a

analysis.name: Donato Cianci
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Cianci is honestly the best math professor I've had at UofM. Even in a large lecture hall, he still manages to be engaging and informative. He doesn't have much control over the rest of the course structure (the labs are pretty bad) but you can tell he really cares about his students.

Very good at explaining material. Very helpful in office hours for homework and concepts and helps make you understand concepts better. Best professor to go to for office hours. Has a great personality and easy to talk to when asking for help with course material. Math 217 is a hard class, but he makes it much easier to understand the concepts.
He was a very engaging professor and was even better outside of class. His office hours were very useful and helped me a lot in the course. I would definitely recommend him for Math 216.

The class structure is a disaster since you don't learn anything from lecture. All you do in class is working in a random team on worksheets for every class. The content is unnecessarily hard, take Math 214 if you can. (RIP stats major) Dan is a very nice guy, but as you see, I'm not sure how good he is at lecturing as he did not lecture in class.

217 is a well-designed class, as discussions and collaboration between students help understanding the materials. Professor Cianci explained the materials clearly and made sure everyone understood. He also gave good hints when we were stuck on worksheet problems. You can never finish the worksheets though, because he will always give you new ones.

analysis.name: Cindy Sowers
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Incredible professor! She is extremely enthusiastic and her lectures are beautifully organized. With some attention and active engagement with readings, papers should be as fun as they are challenging (perhaps more). That said, there will be substantial engagement with religious themes, so if you're not into that you may not enjoy the class.

Cindy is the best professor I've ever had. No question. She's a little quirky (typical for the RC) but her interests are vast and she is extremely knowledgable. If you're at all interested in anything she teaches, take the course. It'll change the way you think. I've taken courses I'm not interested in just to take another course with her.

Cindy is amazing. She's extremely knowledgeable and just too dang cute! RCHums (special topic in Freud) is easily one of the most interesting classes I've taken. The readings are not too hard and all of her lectures thoroughly explain any tricky concepts. I would HIGHLY recommend taking a course with her. She's very enthusiastic!

This class was really brilliant. Lectures were always a presented in an interesting way and generated a lot of good conversation. Cindy assigned three papers spaced fairly evenly throughout the course - never more than 7 pages, but usually 5.

Took this freshman year in a 17-credit semester, expecting it to be really hard. It was hard, but also the high point amidst the other 13 credits. Lectures were engaging and the material was well-selected. Cindy is kind, knowledgeable, and a great teacher, gives good feedback on papers and willing to talk/help outside of class if you're struggling.

analysis.name: Sally Clegg
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor, definitely my favorite from this semester. She is incredibly kind and helpful and will give you very useful feedback. Participation does matter in her grading process but as long as you participate in class, show effort, and generally just show up you are almost guaranteed a good grade.
Sally is a very soft spoken and kind professor who gives constructive feedback and is willing to help when needed.
My goat. Super sweet, can be a tough grader for some projects but nothing crazy. Super understanding and gives great critiques.

Sally was a fantastic professor. She is very methodical and organized in her teaching. There were only a couple of projects in the class, which made grading difficult, but she gave enough time for students to go back and make revisions if they were unhappy with a grade. Be prepared to work frequently outside of class.
She was very well organized and helpful. We learned a solid amount of foundation but was still given plenty of creative freedom.

analysis.name: Herek Clack
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Clack is very knowledgeable. The material can be challenging, especially with 8:30 a.m. lectures three times a week, but having lectures available online helped. I relied on the textbook and office hours, and the guided notes made the content easier to understand. The course takes effort, but Professor Clack is supportive throughout.

While Professor Clack is a caring teacher and nice person, he is a bad professor. His lectures are just talking with fill-the-blank slides not suited for the style of thermo. You have to read the book to learn. He never seems prepared for class, even worse for exams. HW is assigned randomly and solutions/grading seem to have no rubric.

never did practice problems in class just expected you to know how to do them on your own. Just seemed like a research professor who wasn't really there to teach because they wanted to but because they had to.

Good professor. Prepare to spend a lot of time with the problem sets. He expects students to work through the textbook on their own time. Lots of time needed for this class, but he does a decent job lecturing.

The guy is really smart, but he is terrible at explaining things.  His lectures are really hard to follow so you really have to read the book to understand anything.  Homework is confusing, and tests are really hard.  He also is very condescending and not easy to ask questions to- makes you feel bad if you don't understand.

analysis.name: Eleanor Clowney
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I was honestly afraid to take this professor, but I'm glad I signed up for her course. Even though she is lecture heavy, her first exam was fair. Her office hours are great, and she really assists you with the content you're confused about. She appreciates it when students seek help, and she is very passionate about the content she teaches.

She'll start off by giving a simple definition of a topic, and then we will go from 0 to 100 out of no where like it's common knowledge. Impossible to follow in lecture, uses unnecessary terms, goes over 20+ topics in a single lecture, overall terrible teaching style. Only reason to show up is for the mandatory iClicker points. Do not take.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER! TAKE IT WITH SOMEONE ELSE! She doesn't even teach, going over slides extremely fast and in vague detail.
