You have to teach yourself all the material in order to do moderately decent in this class. It's very clear that her knowledge and skill set is more fit for research, not teaching. Run while you can!

I had Professor Clowney for my first half of Biology 172. She convinced me there was something wrong with me. I did everything recommended to succeed, but she taught everything out of order and assumed everyone in the introductory biology class had a Ph.D. in Biology. Her exam questions were purposely meant to confuse you. Avoid at all costs.

She literally reads off of the slides and doesn't elaborate, if she does, it is impossible to understand. Office hours is no help either, if she's discussed something in OH before, she won't go over it again. Worst prof I've EVER had tbh you're in for one if you take her class, although the second prof is much better. Self teach only option to pass

analysis.name: Laura Clapper
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: if i could pick one person to represent the human race to an alien population, i'd pick laura clapper. and the aliens would love us.

Laura is a wonderful professor who truly cares about her students. W300 is self-graded, so as long as you work hard, you'll get an A. Laura has high expectations, but meeting them has significantly improved my writing.

Love, love, LOVE Laura. Take any classes you can with her. One of the most genuine people I have ever met in my life. She is kind without being coddling, and both expects and truly wants the best from her students.

Laura is a wonderful professor, who really cares about her students. She will provide excellent feedback to help you improve your reading, writing, and analytical skills. It's important to participate and stay on top of assignments. If I could take her again, I would.
Just don't take her classes; unsympathetic and not understanding. So many pointless assignments that are time consuming and obnoxious.

analysis.name: Clifford Lampe
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 64 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Ironically, for a class built on gamification, this class is designed really poorly.  Ten 2-4 page writing assignments (which you get little to no helpful feedback for your grade).  2 large projects, 1 semester-long project, weekly pop quizzes (on specific details from the 4 hours worth of reading), final exam.  Don't take this.  HIGHLY SUBJECTIVE

Cliff uses Gradecraft for his class - a program that attempts to turn an academic course at a major university into a video game. The course is structured in a way that is made to let students work at their own pace and instead the teacher drops all of the assignments on you at once. He has planned this class very poorly and I was jk about him hot

Professor Lampe stepped up after our previous professor couldn't teach anymore for personal reasons, and he's been nothing but fair and accommodating. Yes, there were quite a few readings but you really just had to skim them. The tests were also curved so as long as you put in a little effort you'd do well. The final project was also manageable.

Absurd amount of work. 100 + pages of reading per week. obscure pop quiz every week. 10 2-4 page essays, 2 projects equivalent to 10 page essay, another 2500 word essay. no assignments relate to actual material you need to know. will ruin your life. required to go to out of class lectures to complete essays. will be biggest regret of your life.

The GSI's are horrible graders, their feedback is not clear. I don't understand how they grade these assignments. Be prepared for a lot of reading and it will not be helpful for the quizzes. The lectures are very boring. It seems like a lot of the topics are random and do not connect to each other. I wouldn't take this class if not needed.

analysis.name: Claudia Creed
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is really passionate about what she teaches but struggled to connect with students and get them to participate in the class I had. Even so, she always tried her best. Know that she is a slow grader. Would not necessarily recommend.

Decent lecturer. Lots of reading, but it's not THAT deep. Lenient on midnight deadlines which was helpful. Fair grader. Lots of writing (bc it's a writing class), but she's super reasonable and understanding. I was a little scared after reading the single rating on this website, but she's super fair, which is all someone could ask for.

Claudia was a decent lecturer but struggled to engage the class at times. Her one-on-one conferences often lacked clarity, with repeated points filling time rather than offering useful feedback. Her biggest issue was grading delays—waiting six weeks for feedback made it difficult for students who wanted to do redrafts.

Professor Creed is so incredibly nice. She really cares about her students. There's a bit of group work with peer edits. Overall the class was pretty easy with only three essays and very little other work.

- Never graded anything on time. 
- Lectures were boring 
- Accessible outside of class and lenient on deadlines

review_highlights.comment:
(EARTH 351) I learned a TON but the class is a train wreck

-Blames the class for being behind but doesn't make assignments on time
-Labs are HARD AF
-Rude to students in class
-Class order is poor
-Homework is convoluted
-Lectures are FAST, must attend to do well

Clearly well respeced, but horrible teacher.

This is a 2 credit class...and it was one of my worst grades. Not clear about what will be on the exam and exams are extremely hard! I received Cs on two of the three exams and an A on the one when she was absent and we were taught by another prof.  Def dont take this class unless you wanna feel dumb for not doing will in a 2 credit course

Professor Clark seems very nervous at times, and she has difficulty explaining the material.  The quizzes and exams cover material that is not well explained in lecture and cannot be found in the textbook.  Therefore, it is tough to answer some of the questions on the various assignments.  Overall, I do not recommend taking this class.

Marin typifies the very driven/intelligent but also entitled ivy-league-educated academic. When things are not done exactly her way she is RUDE, sometimes boarding on abusive. She tends to be controlling and micromanaging. She lives in an internally generated bubble of constant stress that very few are immune to getting caught up in.

She's really nice and is very passionate about her work. It's annoying that this class is only two credits because you have to study a fair amount to get an A on the exam. If you put in the studying hours, you will get an A.

analysis.name: Henry Cowles
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great professor. He really cares about his students and I feel like I learned a lot. His lectures are really interesting so you should show up. Also super cute and kinda jacked hmu Henry

This guy is great. His classes are very interesting, and he is a great person to chat with in office hours. It's clear that he genuinely cares about his students and his teaching philosophy is very purely academic, with a strong emphasis on learning for it's own sake. Always a joy to go to his class, and I'm excited to take him again!

He's super nice and funny in lecture, you can really tell he loves teaching this subject. His lectures are organized well, but he doesn't really put words on the slides, so notes definitely need to be taken throughout lecture, because the powerpoints will tell you nothing. Would take again, he was amazing!

This class was so easy and Dr. Cowles' lectures were super interesting. There were 2 readings/week that were probably around 40ish pages total. 3 papers, the longest of which is 1500 words. Once a week we did collaborations in lecture, and I really enjoyed these- these mostly involved designing a product or an ad related to our topic for the week.

Professor Cowles is amazing. He truly cares about his students and his lectures are fascinating. He does lecture with little words on the slides, so it's important to listen, but he really is very knowledgeable. Would 100% take this class again!

analysis.name: Charles Severance
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 680 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: He is one of the best Teacher I have seen and one best mentor. May Gol always keep him happy

Class was easy, though I don't feel like I really learned much since everything was online and AI helped out significantly when used correctly. Not sure who this class is for? UX? Took it thinking I would learn SQL/db design, but not the case. Homeworks were easy but could be time consuming. Midterm and final were a breeze. Take if you need 3 CHs

He knows what he talks about. I enjoyed being able to work on the homework tutorials on my own time after I was finished with other prioritized homework. I learned a lot. SI 504 comes in clutch since we use the terminal a lot as well.

I took the Python classes on Amazon/video. When i started I knew absolutly nothing about programing and or computers, I was totaly green, but with his lectures has made it so easy that i keep wondering where was I yesterday. Kudos ! an exceptional teacher, Humble and to the point. Thank you. i'm going to continue with the rest of his classes too.

hey! i am one of the student who is taking coursera classes. the series on python is amazing and the best i have seen so far! awesome knowing this class and thank you a lot for providing us the opportunity to learn online, especially for those of us who do not have privilege to pursue a formal computer class  Thank you again!!

analysis.name: Marcus Collins
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Every lecture feels like a TED Talk - very engaging, but when you ask him to clarify something, he just repeats his TED talk and expects you to understand. This goes for if you ask questions in class or if you go to office hours. 

He is also very accomplished and will make sure you know it, which comes off as full of himself.

While his lectures are inspirational and great.  He grades pretty tough and doesn't grieve feedback on what he grades.  Additionally assignments he graded in our class were graded and returned a week later less that 3 hours in some cases before the next assignment was due.  There was also zero feedback so mistakes were repeated commonly.
hes good and inspirational but lowkey is not a proactive teacher/accessible at all

Multiple huge assignments from very beginning to very end that take forever. You must purchase his book as the main reading for the course. Every class uses the same examples and language from his book. He also doesn't share slides and for projects later in the semester, you are required to incorporate and utilize course concepts

Marcus has a stellar reputation amongst Ross students, and somehow manages to even exceed that reputation. His classes are wildly difficult to get into for a reason. You can tell how much he cares for students to an incredible extent, even going as far as to give his personnel phone number to students. By far the greatest course I have ever taken.

analysis.name: Maria Cotera
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She only lectures half of the semester and the rest is done by GSIs. The readings are a bit boring but you only need to skim them to get good grades on quiz. It is very important to invest effort to section participation and group project (don't make your project boring if you want good grades). Midterm was takehome exam and there was no final exam

Easy to get an A in this class, just skim through the readings for the online quizzes and go to class (but you don't have to take notes because you don't have any tests on lecture material). But I didn't really care for Prof Cotera. She had a pretty heavy bias during lectures and came off as arrogant.

Her graduate level courses are rather boring and are not really engaging. I don't think her teaching style is for me as her class is all over the place. Students who are new to grad school or theory based courses prepare to feel like an imbecile and confused! This comment is based on one of her UT Austin courses

EASY A! But--worst class I've taken at U of M. Opinion based quiz questions, little respect for other epistemological approaches. I'm a liberal, and this was way too far for me. Cherry picking data, little critical thinking, 100 pgs reading/week. Lecture required, no laptops. Belittle opinions. If interested in WOMENSTD, take different course.

She made the lectures interesting and I really liked the class even though I don't agree with everything she taught. My GSI was also very accepting of conflicting viewpoints. There are a lot of readings but you just have to skim them for answers to the online quizzes. The midterm is take home and you work on the final project the whole semester.

analysis.name: Corey Powell
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Corey seems like a cool guy. However, any enjoyment I may have had doing stats had been sucked out of this class. There's an ungodly amount of homework and work you need to do outside of class just to understand the content. I've seen more words than numbers in this class. You also have to learn R coding, which is stupid. I don't recommend!

Please listen to the other people. I was one who thought the other people were being dramatic. It is very important you listen to them and me. Corey Powell makes this class way too complicated for no reason and barely tries to explain it so people understand. review_highlights.comment: The class is def not a lot of work at all, but it is easy to screw up if you don't know the stuff.  Practice exams bear little resemblance to the actual exams and getting an A is by no means a given.  Spillane comes off as very kind and reasonable, but I challenged her poorly worded exams twice and received discourteous emails in response.

The only professor at umich I truly dislike. The class environment was not supportive or encouraging and honestly made me feel uncomfortable and not supported. I have personal experiences that affect my learning and she didn't make me feel like I could share that with her or have her support. She constantly talked down to students unkindly.

Honestly one of the worst professors I've had. She constantly put down students, spoke in a condescending tone, and showed no effort to understand different perspectives. Instead of creating an encouraging learning environment, she made class stressful and unproductive.

A very easy class that counts for the natural science requirement. Homework and class work is only looked at for completion. I thought lectures were interesting, but everyone is different. She has some rules, but they are very easy to follow and conversations can be interesting. Overall, a very easy and good class/teacher.

Unfortunately, I had to take this class in order to graduate. I would completely recommend to stay away if you are not in the same boat. Students, including myself would consistently receive 50-75% on the quizzes/HW assignments despite pulling the information from the literal lecture slides. She also loves to belittle students who ask questions!!!

analysis.name: Dina Gohar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Gohar makes lectures enjoyable and engaging! She explains concepts well with pop culture examples, I didn't miss a single class! I enjoy how Dr Gohar creates a classroom environment where students are encouraged to ask questions. I appreciated the chance to explain what I got wrong on the midterm for partial credit to encourage a growth mindset

I thought Dr. Gohar was a great professor, she was funny and engaging and lectures were always interesting. My only issue with the class were the exams. Sometimes the study guides and exams contained material we haven't learned yet. My advice: please go through all materials given to you, some questions were based on concepts mentioned like once

Dr. Gohar was engaged, but I felt some lectures were all over the place, and there were constant technology issues (obviously, these were not her fault)  that made the class really disorganized. Her GSIs this semester had a hard time explaining concepts during the review sessions and struggled to answer student questions. Very easy overall though.

Word for word reading the slides, majority of the course was covered in the textbook so I still went to class but I didn't need to besides to just know lecture points for the exam. The content was interesting but the slides were also went through quickly, and recordings only available with advance request. Very easy though.

Dr. Gohar is kind, approachable, and very knowledgeable on the subject and does a good job making lectures intriguing. As far as the class goes, there is definitely a lot of content, but is manageable if you study. Overall, this was a great course and I hope to take another class with Dr. Gohar in the future!

analysis.name: Evangelos Dimou
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dimou provides all the materials you need to succeed: detailed notes, clear lectures, ample office hours. He's welcoming of questions and doesn't not seem burdened when you need extra help. MATH 3100 was a lot of content and had some confusing concepts, but if you come in ready to work, you'll be fine. Enjoyed this class and this professor!
Prepare to teach yourself all the content. He's a nice guy and he does try I just don't think he's a very naturally gifted teacher. TA was lowkey hot
Take this class if you love math and greek accents. Ratings range from "he's cool I guess" and "he's good about office hours" to "don't take this class it's very hard."
Dr. Dimou was a good teacher. Lectured clearly. Super stingy with partial credit. Luckily the final grade was comprised of a lot of homework and participation
I really did not enjoy his teaching and I feel like I taught myself the entire class

analysis.name: Chris DiScenza
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is extremely nice, and each review my peers and I have tried to leave has been removed. I think he sees these and requests them to be taken down. Nice, but cannot teach at all. Concepts taught are frequently slightly different than the homework, masteries, and exams. He confuses more than teaches.

Chris is super caring and kind. Lectures were a bit confusing, so be prepared to do some extra learning outside of class. Chris cares so much about his students and was willing to stay after office hours to help.

I'm pretty good at math so 105 wasn't hard for me, but it prob would be hard if you have no basis in precalc. Some people felt like he was confusing. He explains math in terms of concepts and wants you to understand the "why" and not just memorize. He's super nice, responds to emails, will stay later in office hours for you, cares abt students

analysis.name: Kimberly Diaz
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Honestly one of the best professors I've ever had! The course is hard and can be stressful if you fall behind, especially as I was also taking EECS 280 at the same time. However, Prof. Diaz is very supportive and caring, and wants to help you succeed in the class. She explains lecture material clearly and explains worksheets throughout each class.

Diaz is an amazing lecturer! 203 tends to be very difficult to understand at first, but she does a great job of breaking concepts down and making them easy to understand. I wasn't registered for her section, but went to her lectures as often as I could. I would recommend her the most out of any of the 203 lecturers.

Professor Diaz is an amazing lecturer. She truly cares about the experience of her students and is really clear in how she teaches. The class was not the easiest, but she definitely made it more manageable. The class had a homework and a checkpoint every week, which sometimes took a bit of time.

Prof Diaz is an amazing lecturer and her annotated slides and handouts made difficult topics so much easier to understand! She also makes it worth it to come to lecture in person over the recordings giving time to work with others on problems and build a community! This class is difficult but she made it accessible and enjoyable!
difficult content, but a very good lecturer that made me feel prepared

analysis.name: Gregory Dick
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Dick is a good lecturer. Every lecture is about a new subject, and you rarely get a boring lecture. For participation, the class uses iClicker, which mine didn't track the location (use this information at your discretion). Weekly quizzes are easy and a quick search. The exam was a compilation of the quiz questions, so studying was easy.

He is fantastic and this is exactly what a half-semester mini-course should be. Lectures were interesting and engaging. Class was structured in a way that makes it impossible to do poorly unless you actively avoid the class material. If you're looking for a light class for one more credit with an amazing professor, this is it.

Good lecturer, but the material covered is pretty dense and sometimes hard to focus on for the entire 1.5 hour lecture.  Weekly quizzes are pretty easy.  Slides are very helpful and contain most of the information needed.  Greg is super nice and helpful.  I would take another class with him in a heartbeat if microbial life didn't drive me bonkers.

His half of Earth 313 was really easy to understand and he provided a clear guideline of what we needed to know for exams. His lectures could be a bit boring after a while, but if you're passionate about the topic, he is a good source to get information from. Overall, an excellent professor who listens to students and works well with them.

Gregory Dick is a great professor. He is very easy to listen to and really wants to make sure that everyone understands what he's teaching. Very approachable and the lectures are helpful, though a lot of people skip lecture and do fine (all the lecture slides are on ctools). I would definitely recommend taking a class with this professor.

analysis.name: Dmitry Stolyarov
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It was his first time teaching the course and he clearly wasn't prepared. He didn't know how to help us study to his tests. We didn't have any practice exams to go off of or review sessions. The homework is lengthy and very difficult. His slides are very disorganized and hard to follow. He is very boring in lecture. I fell asleep. Don't take him.

Good luck not falling asleep in his lecture. Good luck understanding the questions he asks in homework and exam.  Good luck with the "interesting" grading system.  Good luck distinguish notation from 3 different resources.   If anyone is up for the experience of failing a major class, do not miss out on him.
Hard exams and hard homework, avoid if you can.

I'll give him a little leeway since he says it's his first time teaching the course. That being said, he's made the course very difficult. The materials that we're using keep changing, you really need both textbooks to do well, homeworks are REALLY difficult compared to 401, and the grading scale is really strange. Go to office hours, and go often.

His lectures were confusing and hard to follow in class.  He had ok lecture notes on Ctools but they were from many years ago so they didn't necessarily follow the lecture from this year.  You only count one midterm and homework helps to weight how your midterm and final, so the grading is decent but I only got by because the GSI was awesome.

analysis.name: Dmitriy Boyarchenko
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Mitya's class is extremely hard, and you should be sure that you want to work hard before enrolling. That being said, he is the most helpful and clear Professors in all of the land. His interest and faith in his students is limitless. He will never make you feel inadequate or stupid, and will always be there to help.
He was very kind and accomodating. He also helped me on outside course work.

Mitya is really cool.  Considering how hard the course is, he makes it fairly easy to understand.  In addition, if you do the homework and all, you are guarenteed an A, so even if you find it impossible, just stick with it and try your best, and you'll do fine

Had Mitya for 395-6.  Taught the material in his own order using his own notes to great positive effect.  Learned everything I needed to know for the classes I'm now in (596 especially).  He also has great jokes.
Mitya is swag // he's so cool i can brag // his classes you should take // a math major you will make // and honors math is so fly // i will hate to say good-bye.

analysis.name: Lisa Disch
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 104 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Mandatory attendance for lectures where Disch never finishes slide decks and barely discusses content from the readings. Lectures only to ask students for opinions, then shares her own biased opinion, instead of teaching. Recycles lots of outdated materials. Do NOT take POLSCI with Disch if you actually want to learn political theory. GSI saved me.

Mandatory attendance for lectures that are nothing but a waste of time. Instead of teaching, Disch only calls on hands from students asking for opinions, meaning that slide decks are never completed in class, are extremely vague and barely related to the reading/reading quizzes. If you wish to ACTUALLY learn anything, do not take Disch's POLSCI101.

Very engaging lectures, great sense of humor. Political theory isn't exactly the most fun topic, but she still makes it exciting by incorporating our opinions and writing into the lectures. Easy to get an A, a lot of your grade is automatically 100% for participation/submitting assignments, only two assignments that really get graded on a rubric.

Extremely easy class. Lisa Disch is a very easy professor and a very nice woman, but I feel like she was not even trying to challenge us. She usually ended class about half an hour early, which makes everyone happy, but it also gives the impression that she doesn't take teaching seriously. Oh well, political theory is a useless topic anyway.

Professor Disch is AMAZING. The class itself is very easy. She doesn't believe in exams so there are none. There's just one group paper and an individual final project. Class gets let out 30 minutes early because part of homework is watching lecture videos that are usually just 20 minutes long. Definitely recommend this class for anyone!
